title: Optical Signature of Bias-Induced Carrier Injection in a WSe2/MoS2 Heterostructure Diode
abstract: We investigate the bias-dependent photoluminescence (PL) response of a WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructure diode. Under forward bias, trion-related emission in WSe$_2$ is markedly enhanced, whereas reverse bias produces minimal spectral changes. This asymmetric response cannot be explained by electric-field effects alone and instead reflects carrier injection at the functional interface. These results demonstrate that PL provides a direct optical probe of carrier injection in an operating van der Waals heterostructure. More broadly, this approach establishes spatially resolved PL spectroscopy as a versatile tool for pinpointing the interfaces governing device operation in van der Waals heterostructures.

summaries.en: Bias-dependent photoluminescence measurements of a WSe2/MoS2 heterostructure diode reveal that forward bias markedly enhances trion-related emission in WSe2 while reverse bias produces minimal spectral changes, indicating that photoluminescence directly probes carrier injection at the functional interface rather than electric-field effects alone.
summaries.zh: 对WSe2/MoS2异质结二极管进行的偏压依赖光致发光测量表明，正向偏压显著增强WSe2中与三激子相关的发光，而反向偏压几乎不引起光谱变化，说明光致发光可直接探测功能界面处的载流子注入，而不仅是电场效应。

title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The calculated dielectric functions, refractive indices, absorption coefficients, reflectivity, optical conductivities, and electron energy-loss spectra reveal systematic changes in optical response across the chalcogen series. The absorption onset shifts toward lower photon energies, from approximately 2.4 eV in Y2CdS4 to 1.7 eV in Y2CdTe4. Thermoelectric calculations indicate promising Seebeck coefficients and power factors, with Y2CdSe4 exhibiting a favorable balance of transport properties. Charge-density distributions, electron localization functions, and Bader charge analyses suggest increasing covalent bonding contributions from sulfide to telluride. These findings highlight the potential of Y2CdX4 compounds for tunable optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications.

title: Fabry-Pérot Cavity formed by Magnonic waveguide using holes and notches
abstract: In this paper, we have investigated a spin-wave-based Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity using two air holes and notches embedded in a magnonic waveguide. Through micromagnetic simulations, we have demonstrated the spin-wave profile, as well as the transmission and reflection spectra of the FP type magnonic waveguide, by varying the distance between the center of holes and notches. We have introduced an analysis of the reflection spectra in an FP type magnonic waveguide, which is essential and considerable for the performance of magnonic integrated circuits. We have also presented a theoretical model to describe the transmission and reflection characteristics of the FP-type magnonic waveguide. Furthermore, active tuning of the resonance peak of the FP type magnonic wavguide by varying the external magnetic field has been demonstrated. Our proposed structure and its study may contribute to the development of magnonic integrated circuits for low-power computing and data processing in next-generation spintronic technologies.

title: The Agentic AI Kerr Lab: LLM Agents for Kerr Microscopy Experiments with Magnetic Skyrmions
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are topological spin textures that can be observed directly by magnetic microscopy and driven by fields and currents, which makes them a model system for fundamental physics and candidates for spintronic devices. Magneto-optical Kerr microscopy is a method to image them in real time; however, most experiments use an inefficient cycle of consecutive imaging, analysis and excitation in which every step requires the judgement of the experimentalist operating the setup. Here we present the Agentic AI Kerr Lab (AgentKerr), in which an agent based on a large language model operates this cycle automatically and efficiently on a Kerr microscope. Rather than relying on pattern detection by a language model, a convolutional neural network trained on Kerr images turns live images into skyrmion observables such as position, size and shape, on which the agent bases its decisions. The architecture lets agents operate the instruments safely, as every hardware action is checked deterministically against an action policy, independently of the agent that issues it. With no procedure given, the agent determines by itself how to create, tune and move skyrmions, and writes its own analyses. The approach can be transferred to other spin textures and points towards magnetic imaging experiments in which the researcher poses the question and the agent finds the way to realize the experiments that yield the answer.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Applied Physics (physics.app-ph)

summaries.en: The authors introduce AgentKerr, an LLM-based agent that autonomously operates a magneto-optical Kerr microscope for magnetic skyrmion experiments, using a convolutional neural network to convert live Kerr images into skyrmion observables that guide its decisions, with all hardware actions checked deterministically against an action policy for safety.

title: Quantum dynamics of ultrasmall magnetic skyrmions in atomic-defect landscapes
abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are prime candidates for future information technology, and their fate in devices is settled by the defects they encounter. In ultrathin films, skyrmions can be as small as a couple of nanometers, carrying only a few tens of magnetic moments, while atomic defects reshape their energy landscape on the atomic scale. Here, we demonstrate that such ultrasmall skyrmions can behave quantum mechanically and that their quantum dynamics is unusual. Since the gyrotropic force dominates, the two coordinates of a ferromagnetic skyrmion are canonically conjugate and the skyrmion behaves as a particle in the lowest Landau level of an effective magnetic field, with a magnetic length of 0.6~Å. Utilizing skyrmion-defect interaction profiles of Cr and Fe adatoms and dimers in PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from atomistic spin simulations parametrized from first principles, we unveil quantized gyrotropic orbits with level spacings of 20--85~$\mu$eV, bound not only by pinning defects but also, counter-intuitively, by repulsive ones. Saddle points of the energy landscape act as quantum beam splitters for skyrmions, and quantum depinning reaches rates of 1--100~Hz below the critical current. Embedded impurities, in contrast, bind the skyrmion so strongly that it ceases to behave as a rigid particle, defining a strong-coupling regime. For the Gilbert damping typical of ultrathin films, the quantized levels remain well resolved. The thermal-to-quantum crossover lies between 40 and 160~mK, which is within reach of millikelvin scanning tunneling microscopy, where tip-induced escape statistics and electron spin resonance STM can reveal the quantized gyrotropic motion of skyrmions pinned at defects crafted atom by atom.

title: Multistable elastic pixels: nematic elasticity for non-volatile positioning of colloidal optical scatterers
abstract: Non-volatile reconfiguration of optical devices, in which a configuration persists without continuous energy input, remains a challenge. We introduce multistable elastic pixels (MEPs), lithographically defined pores filled with a nematic liquid crystal, whose curved ends capture a scattering inclusion in one of two mechanically stable sites. Simulations and experiments show that pore geometry and homeotropic surface anchoring define the energy minima and the height of the barrier between them. This barrier far exceeds thermal energies, stabilizing a scatterer location absent an external field. Colloidal inclusions switch reversibly between sites under transient electric fields. Using arrays of static scatterers, we show that the two positional states produce distinct responses at visible wavelengths, demonstrating the potential of MEPs for reconfigurable devices and metasurfaces. Unlike phase-change and liquid-crystal-tuned approaches, which switch a material surrounding fixed scatterers, MEPs use the nematoelastic energy landscape to move the optical element itself.

summaries.en: Multistable elastic pixels use lithographically defined nematic liquid crystal-filled pores whose curved ends create two mechanically stable sites for a colloidal scatterer, with a nematoelastic energy barrier far exceeding thermal energy that enables non-volatile, field-switchable positioning and distinct visible-wavelength optical responses.
summaries.zh: 多稳态弹性像素利用光刻定义的、填充向列相液晶的孔洞，其弯曲末端为胶体散射体提供两个机械稳定位置，并由远超热能的向列弹性势垒实现无场保持的非易失性定位和电场可逆切换，从而在可见波段产生不同的光学响应。

title: A Julia implementation of Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation in periodic systems
abstract: We present a flexible Julia codebase implementing Floquet-Bloch theory for high-harmonic generation (HHG) in periodic tight-binding systems. Using the frequency-domain Fourier-Sambe formalism, the package maps the time-dependent Schroedinger equation onto a static eigenvalue problem. This allows direct computation of Floquet states, quasienergy bands, and harmonic currents for 1D, 2D, or 3D lattices under arbitrary light polarizations. The implementation supports both analytical Fourier-Bessel expansions (via Peierls substitution) and numerical Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT). We validate the code against a canonical 1D two-band model and showcase its capabilities on 2D honeycomb systems: gapped graphene mapping HHG cutoff scaling with hopping parameters and the Kane-Mele model, exploring field-induced quasienergy gaps and topological transitions under linear and circular driving fields. In addition to the theoretical presentation, we provide a flexible and efficient open-source Julia implementation of the Floquet formalism: this https URL .

summaries.en: The paper presents an open-source Julia codebase that implements the frequency-domain Fourier-Sambe Floquet-Bloch formalism for computing Floquet states, quasienergy bands, and high-harmonic currents in 1D, 2D, and 3D periodic tight-binding lattices under arbitrary light polarization, validated on a 1D two-band model and applied to gapped graphene and the Kane-Mele model.
summaries.zh: 本文介绍了一个开源 Julia 代码库，它实现了频域 Fourier-Sambe Floquet-Bloch 形式，用于在任意光偏振下计算一维、二维和三维周期性紧束缚晶格中的 Floquet 态、准能带和高次谐波电流，并在一维双带模型上进行了验证，还应用于有带隙石墨烯和 Kane-Mele 模型。

title: Nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity driven by charge fluctuations in monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$
abstract: Monolayer FeSe and Fe(Te,Se) grown on SrTiO$_3$ exhibit some of the highest superconducting transition temperatures among iron-based superconductors, yet their pairing mechanism and symmetry remain elusive. Motivated by the recent surprising discovery of nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM) [T. Wei et al., arXiv:2610.38421 (2026)], we investigate superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$3$ (1L-FeSe/STO) within an extended Hubbard model incorporating both onsite and intersite Coulomb interactions among Fe $3d$ and Se $4p$ orbitals. We show that Fe-Se intersite Coulomb repulsion strongly enhances small-momentum $p$-$d$ charge-transfer fluctuations, which mediate attractive intraorbital spin-singlet pairing interactions. These electronic fluctuations may be further enhanced by forward-scattering optical phonons of the SrTiO$3$ substrate. The resulting intrapocket attraction, together with residual repulsive interpocket interactions, stabilizes a mirror-odd, nodeless $B_{1g}$ ($d$-wave) superconducting state with opposite gap signs on the two electron pockets. Both Fe $t_{2g}$ and Se $4p$ orbitals contribute substantially to this multiorbital superconductivity. The calculated superconducting gap and density of states exhibit a two-peak structure, while the Josephson tunneling conductance displays a half-lattice-period modulation, in excellent agreement with experimental observations. Our results establish electronic charge-transfer fluctuations as a viable pairing mechanism for unconventional nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/STO.

summaries.en: An extended Hubbard model including Fe 3d and Se 4p orbitals shows that Fe-Se intersite Coulomb repulsion enhances small-momentum p-d charge-transfer fluctuations, which mediate intraorbital spin-singlet pairing and stabilize a mirror-odd nodeless B1g d-wave state in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO3, reproducing the two-peak gap/DOS structure and half-lattice-period Josephson conductance modulation seen experimentally.
summaries.zh: 包含Fe 3d与Se 4p轨道的扩展Hubbard模型表明，Fe-Se间位库仑排斥会增强小动量p-d电荷转移涨落，进而介导轨道内自旋单重态配对，使单层FeSe/SrTiO3稳定在镜面奇宇称的无节点B1g d波态，并重现了实验观测到的双峰能隙/态密度结构以及半晶格周期的约瑟夫森电导调制。
summaries.ja: Fe 3d軌道とSe 4p軌道を含む拡張ハバード模型により、Fe-Se間の異サイトクーロン反発が小運動量のp-d電荷移動揺らぎを強め、これが軌道内スピン一重項 pairing を媒介して単層FeSe/SrTiO3において鏡面奇パリティのノードレスB1g d波状態を安定化し、実験で観測された二峰性のギャップ・状態密度構造と半格子周期のジョセフソン伝導度変調を再現することを示した。

title: Three-Dimensional FDTD Simulation of Superconducting Terahertz Emitters Using an Effective Medium Approximation
abstract: Compact and tunable terahertz (THz) sources with controllable polarization are sought for high-speed links, spectroscopy, and imaging. In superconducting THz emitters based on a cuprate Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+\delta}$, which have the potential to satisfy such properties, modeling often relies on heavy nonlinear solvers or empirical isotropic dielectrics, obscuring anisotropy, plasma response, and bias dependence. We derive an anisotropic, dispersive effective permittivity from the Lawrence-Doniach model for a layered superconductor and implement it as a user-defined material in a commercial Finite-difference Time-domain (FDTD) solver. Simulations of two device geometries reproduce linearly polarized emission from a rectangular mesa and low-axial-ratio (near-circular) emission from a truncated square mesa. This CAD-ready workflow links superconducting theory to device design, enabling rapid searches and parameter optimization for next-generation THz sources.

summaries.en: An anisotropic, dispersive effective permittivity derived from the Lawrence-Doniach model for layered superconductors is implemented as a user-defined material in a commercial FDTD solver, reproducing linearly polarized emission from a rectangular mesa and low-axial-ratio near-circular emission from a truncated square mesa in superconducting Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ terahertz emitters.
summaries.zh: 该研究从层状超导体的Lawrence-Doniach模型推导出各向异性色散有效介电常数，并将其作为用户自定义材料实现在商用FDTD求解器中，模拟重现了Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ超导太赫兹发射器中矩形台面的线偏振发射和截角方形台面的低轴比近圆偏振发射。
summaries.ja: 層状超伝導体のLawrence-Doniach模型から異方性・分散性の実効誘電率を導出し、商用FDTDソルバーのユーザー定義材料として実装することで、Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ超伝導テラヘルツ発振器において矩形メサからの直線偏光放射と切り欠き角を持つ正方形メサからの低軸比（ほぼ円偏光）放射を再現した。

title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. Our experiments further reveal a boundary-associated redistribution of the transport field when bias is applied along the $a$-axis, suggesting a possible role of crystal boundaries in charge transport along the low-conductivity direction. This work establishes bias-dependent KPFM as a powerful platform for uncovering localized transport phenomena in low-symmetry quantum materials.

summaries.en: Bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy combined with anisotropic transport simulations directly visualizes crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles and boundary-associated field redistribution along the low-conductivity a-axis in CrSBr.
summaries.zh: 结合偏压依赖性开尔文探针力显微镜与各向异性输运模拟，该研究直接可视化了CrSBr中随晶向变化的电势分布，以及沿低电导率a轴方向与边界相关的输运场重新分布。
summaries.ja: バイアス依存ケルビンプローブフォース顕微鏡と異方性輸送シミュレーションを組み合わせることで、CrSBrにおいて結晶方位に依存する電位分布と、低導電率a軸方向のバイアス印加時に生じる境界に起因した輸送電場の再分布を直接可視化した。

title: Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice: a tricritical bridge from square to kagome
abstract: Artificial spin ices (ASIs) are arrays of interacting nanomagnets in which phase transitions can be imaged and controlled. Studies of the thermodynamic have focused mainly on the square and kagome lattices, and on their variants. Here we study artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice, formed of squares and octagons. At fixed lattice constant, the ratio $r$ of the square and octagon link lengths tunes the interactions strongly while changing the geometry only slightly. Magnetic force microscopy and Monte Carlo simulations show a continuous bridge from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior. At small $r$ the system has a single ordering transition, whereas at large $r$ it passes from a correlated paramagnet to charge order and then long-range order. The two regimes meet in a multicritical region, accurately modeled by a Blume-Capel model of the octagon toroidal moments. From this picture, we design a comparative magnetometry protocol that unambiguously separates interaction effects from single-nanomagnet effects in thermally active samples. Finally, the charge-ordered region maps onto a tunable dimer model, with a Coulomb phase and pinch points along the line between two ordered dimer phases. The CaVO ASI thus provides access to a rich phase diagram only through geometric tuning, without requiring extreme experimental conditions.

summaries.en: Artificial spin ice on the CaVO lattice tunes the ratio of square and octagon link lengths to bridge continuously from square-ice-like to kagome-like behavior, meeting in a multicritical region well modeled by a Blume-Capel model of octagon toroidal moments and enabling a magnetometry protocol that separates interaction from single-nanomagnet effects and a charge-ordered regime mapping onto a tunable dimer model with a Coulomb phase.
summaries.zh: CaVO晶格上的人工自旋冰通过调节正方形与八边形链路长度之比，从类方格冰行为连续过渡到类笼目冰行为，并在多临界区相遇，该区域可用八边形环向矩的Blume-Capel模型准确描述，由此还可设计磁测量方案以区分相互作用效应与单纳米磁体效应，且电荷有序区可映射为具有库仑相的可调二聚体模型。
summaries.ja: CaVO格子上の人工スピンアイスでは、正方形と八角形のリンク長比を変えることでスクエアアイス的挙動からカゴメ的挙動へ連続的に橋渡しされ、両領域は八角形トロイダルモーメントのBlume-Capel模型で精度よく記述されるマルチクリティカル領域で出会い、これにより相互作用効果と単一ナノ磁石効果を分離する磁気測定プロトコルや、クーロン相を持つ可変ダイマーモデルへ写像される電荷秩序領域が得られる。

title: Plasmon modes in three-dimensional multifold semimetals. II. Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl and Kramers-Weyl nodes
abstract: We investigate collective charge excitations in three-dimensional multifold semimetals in which multiple bands cross the Fermi level at a positive chemical potential, focusing on pseudospin-3/2 Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl semimetals and on Kramers-Weyl semimetals. Both systems host multiple concentric Fermi surfaces at positive chemical potential. Within the random-phase approximation, we analyse the density response, Drude weights, dielectric function, plasmon modes and their Landau damping, and Friedel oscillations, considering both small and arbitrary momentum transfers. In our companion work, arXiv:2610.18629 , we investigated pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals, with and without a quadratic correction to their dispersion, as well as Hopf and Weyl semimetals. Comparing these systems allows us to elucidate the distinct roles of band dispersions and eigenstates in shaping collective charge dynamics. Our results demonstrate that collective charge excitations can distinguish multifold nodes with multiple Fermi surfaces and reveal information encoded in their eigenstates beyond that contained in the single-particle dispersion.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; High Energy Physics - Theory (hep-th)

summaries.en: Within the random-phase approximation, the authors analyze density response, Drude weights, dielectric function, plasmon modes and their Landau damping, and Friedel oscillations in pseudospin-3/2 Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl and Kramers-Weyl semimetals with multiple concentric Fermi surfaces, showing that collective charge excitations can distinguish multifold nodes and reveal eigenstate information beyond the single-particle dispersion.
summaries.zh: 作者在随机相位近似下分析了具有多重同心费米面的赝自旋-3/2 Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl半金属和Kramers-Weyl半金属的密度响应、Drude权重、介电函数、等离激元模式及其朗道阻尼以及Friedel振荡，表明集体电荷激发能够区分多重节点并揭示单粒子色散之外的本征态信息。
summaries.ja: 著者らはランダム位相近似の下で、複数の同心フェルミ面を持つ擬スピン3/2のRarita-Schwinger-Weyl半金属およびKramers-Weyl半金属の密度応答、Drude重み、誘電関数、プラズモンモードとそのランダウ減衰、Friedel振動を解析し、集団電荷励起が多重点を識別し、単一粒子分散を超えた固有状態の情報を明らかにできることを示した。

title: Superradiance fingerprints of moiré exciton-biexciton condensates: path-entangled biphoton vs. supercurrent-enabled one-photon channel
abstract: Hybrid moiré excitons form a dense array of electrically tunable single-photon emitters, entailing cooperative optical responses with intriguing consequences. With the strong dipole-dipole interaction, they also realize Bose-Hubbard quantum simulators of emergent correlated matter such as Bose-Einstein condensates (BEC). Here we reveal the characteristic cooperative radiation from condensates of hybrid moiré excitons in twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayers. In each individual moiré trap, the layer hybridization selection rule dictates that the ground-state exciton is a quantum emitter of orbital-angular-momentum photons, with an exceptionally long radiative lifetime. Ground-state emission becomes pronounced only upon forming condensates, where inter-sublattice dipole attraction and intra-sublattice repulsion together lead to the coexistence of exciton and biexciton BEC with comparable weights. The biexciton (molecular-type) BEC decays through superradiance of path-entangled biphotons, whereas the exciton (atomic-type) BEC is dark at rest and becomes superradiant when it carries a supercurrent. Our findings not only uncover a novel source of entangled light but also establish unique fingerprints for exploring the cold chemistry of atomic-molecular condensates with moiré excitons.

title: Structural and Optical Properties of PVP-Modified ZnS Nanoparticles for Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
abstract: Pristine and PVP-modified ZnS nanoparticles were investigated to examine how PVP addition affects structural, surface, optical, and methylene blue (MB) decolorization properties. X-ray diffraction confirmed cubic zinc-blende ZnS in all samples, with apparent Scherrer coherent-domain sizes of 3.10-3.31 nm. Electron microscopy revealed agglomeration, while HRTEM and electron diffraction confirmed locally crystalline regions in S1 and S4. The estimated direct Tauc gap decreased from 3.69 eV for S1 to 3.58 eV for S4. Between 100 and 300 K, the principal TO-like Raman band softened on heating, while visible photoluminescence changed predominantly within the overlapping green-yellow region. After 210 min under 254 nm irradiation, MB-band losses near 664 nm reached 19.33%, 58.18%, 70.00%, and 94.42% for S1-S4, compared with 6.58% for the catalyst-free control. PVP modification therefore alters optical and dye-decolorization responses while preserving the principal ZnS phase; however, dye-band attenuation alone does not establish complete mineralization.

title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
abstract: We investigated how the bias-voltage-dependent variation in the ferroelectric domain switching pathways affects the transient negative capacitance in multidomain PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains having, primarily, 90$^\circ$ walls. Using the vector piezoresponse force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, we show that, together with strain, local variation in composition results in the formation of labyrinthine domains in epitaxial films of thickness $\sim$1 $\mu$m. Clear signature of emergence of bias-voltage-dependent pathways could be observed in the Raman modes exhibiting splitting due to an intermediate state - different from the initial and final states - at the ``intermediate state of switching". The polarization relaxation patterns also show different states emerging depending on the bias voltage characteristics. The phase-field simulation of relaxation of ``intermediate state of switching" corroborates the experimental results and also exhibits dependence of the domain-wall area on the bias voltage and damping parameter. Combining the results of experiments and theoretical calculation, we show, therefore, that the variation of bias voltage leads to a change in the domain switching pathways and each pathway is associated with specific domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching". Since, the net domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching" governs the magnitude of transient negative capacitance, this work thus traces the origin of tunability of transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor.

title: Disorder, Interactions, and the Fate of the Two-Dimensional Electron System: Wigner Crystal, Metal-Insulator Transition, and Amorphous Solid
abstract: We present a unified theoretical study of the interplay between Coulomb disorder and Coulomb interactions in two-dimensional electron systems, covering the Wigner crystallization transition, the metal-insulator transition, and the crossover from a Wigner crystal to an amorphous localized solid in both zero magnetic field and the lowest Landau level. Using Hartree-Fock theory, variational Monte Carlo, and percolation and strong-localization arguments, we show that quenched charged disorder destroys true long-range Wigner crystalline order in the thermodynamic limit at any nonzero charged-impurity density, within the Imry-Ma-Larkin framework; the finite-system density image is that of an amorphous solid with crystalline coherence over at most a few lattice spacings. For the two-dimensional metal-insulator transition we show, in a controlled nonlinear-Thomas-Fermi model of long-range Coulomb disorder at setback d, that the half-depletion density of the semiclassical landscape and the Ioffe-Regel-Mott density of Born-RPA transport track each other to within a factor of order unity over the physically relevant range of impurity density and setback, with a slow n_i^(-1/10) d^(-1/5) spread; the agreement reflects the common energy scale E_dis ~ E_F at the transition rather than a theorem, and modest independent short-range transport channels can shift the ratio by factors of order two. The article is a theoretical study under well-defined approximations; it takes the recent scanning tunneling microscopy imaging experiments on two-dimensional electron systems and the longstanding disorder-versus-interaction debate on the two-dimensional metal-insulator transition as motivation, and leaves to the reader the comparison between its calculated signatures and the published experimental analyses.
subjects: Strongly Correlated Electrons (cond-mat.str-el) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

summaries.en: This theoretical study argues that quenched charged disorder destroys true long-range Wigner crystalline order at any nonzero impurity density in two-dimensional electron systems, yielding instead an amorphous solid with only short-range crystalline coherence, and shows that the half-depletion density and the Ioffe-Regel-Mott density track each other within a factor of order unity across the metal-insulator transition.

title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. With our approach, we show that populating quantum dots does not require engineered reservoirs, source/drain bias, ohmic contacts, or in-situ doping. As a result, the number of gates can be kept minimal and the fabrication process can be simplified. Moreover, this approach can be applied to a wide range of direct-bandgap semiconductor quantum dot systems. This hybrid device demonstration is a first step towards a different scalability approach for quantum dot arrays.

summaries.en: The authors demonstrate a gate-defined double quantum dot in an undoped GaAs substrate by using above-gap laser illumination to generate and separate photo-carriers that are trapped beneath accumulation gates, with charge readout performed by an on-chip superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator, showing that quantum dots can be populated without engineered reservoirs, source/drain bias, ohmic contacts, or in-situ doping.

title: Modeling Crystallization in Concentrated Suspensions of Compressible Microgels
abstract: Soft colloidal particles, such as microgels, made of cross-linked polymer gels that can swell by absorbing a good solvent, have internal degrees of freedom that allow them to respond to external stimuli by changing size. Sensitive responses to variations in temperature and concentration have inspired many practical applications, e.g., to drug delivery, biosensing, filtration, and photonic crystals. At sufficiently high concentrations, mutual crowding can drive microgels to interpenetrate or deform by faceting. To explore the influence of particle softness and compressibility on thermodynamic phase stability, we develop a coarse-grained model in which spherical microgels interact via the Hertz elastic pair potential and can respond to crowding by deswelling and faceting or interpenetrating, as governed by the Flory-Rehner theory of polymer networks. In our model, faceting reduces the volume available for swelling, while interpenetration affects polymer solvent mixing entropy. By performing Monte Carlo simulations that incorporate novel trial changes in particle size and shape, we compute equilibrium swelling ratios and Lindemann ratios to determine the fluid-solid phase stability boundary over a range of particle softness, tuned by varying cross-link fraction. Predictions from our facet model are in qualitative agreement with experiments and molecular-scale simulations. In contrast to the phase behavior of incompressible Hertzian spheres, we find that suspensions of compressible microgels crystallize at significantly lower volume fractions when accounting for the free energy costs of faceting and interpenetration. Our results extend previous studies of microgel phase behavior and can help to interpret experiments.

summaries.en: A coarse-grained model combining the Hertz pair potential with Flory-Rehner theory and Monte Carlo simulations shows that compressible microgels, which can deswell, facet, or interpenetrate under crowding, crystallize at significantly lower volume fractions than incompressible Hertzian spheres when the free energy costs of faceting and interpenetration are included.

title: Ferroelectric Switching in x-cut MgO-doped Thin-Film Lithium Niobate: Implications for Periodic Poling and Domain-Wall Electronics
abstract: Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) revives a mature ferroelectric as a wafer-scale platform for integrated photonics and, increasingly, for domain-wall electronics such as nonvolatile memories and memristors. Both applications rely on controlled ferroelectric switching, which is poorly understood in TFLN: periodic poling consistently requires electric fields above 30~kV/mm, far above the coercive fields of about 21~kV/mm and 4.5~kV/mm of bulk congruent and 5~mol\% MgO-doped lithium niobate, respectively. Here, we present systematic ferroelectric hysteresis measurements on x-cut, 5~mol\% MgO-doped TFLN with coplanar electrodes as used for periodic poling, combining the positive-up-negative-down (PUND) method with second-harmonic microscopy (SHM). We obtain a spontaneous polarization of $(0.72\pm0.02)$~C/m$^2$, consistent with bulk values, while the coercive field varies between 24 and 40~kV/mm with the voltage ramp rate and depends on the electrode geometry. We identify three contributions to the high coercive fields: (i) fast voltage ramps, (ii) finger electrodes, and (iii) the coplanar surface-electrode geometry. Together with bulk data, the coercive field follows a single power law of the ramp rate over five orders of magnitude, showing that the high fields are dominated by switching dynamics rather than by intrinsic thin-film properties. Moreover, the apparent internal field depends on the electrode geometry, and reverse switching leaves buried, electrically isolated domains. These results provide guidelines for scalable, fab-compatible periodic poling---one of the principal bottlenecks of TFLN device integration---and for the write and erase operation of TFLN domain-wall devices.

title: Imaging the Current Distribution in Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensors with Scanning SQUID Microscopy
abstract: Transition-edge sensors (TESs) exploit the resistive transition of a superconductor to detect minute changes in temperature. While significant progress has been made in understanding the temperature- and current-dependent resistive transition in these devices, important aspects of TES behavior under bias remain unresolved. In particular, existing TES models largely neglect spatial variations in the superconducting state and current distribution arising from device geometry and proximity effects associated with the superconducting leads and normal metal features. Using scanning superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) microscopy (SSM), we directly image local superconducting properties and transport current in two molybdenum-gold (MoAu) X-ray TES designs. We measure the local diamagnetic response to identify superconducting regions in devices voltage-biased within the transition and the Oersted field generated by the transport current to reconstruct the corresponding current distribution. We observe bias-dependent reconfigurations of the current distribution that track current-induced changes in superconducting regions, highlighting the importance of mesoscale spatial variations for TES device physics, operation, and design.

title: Observation of Superconductivity in a Cu-Rich High-Entropy Alloy
abstract: A Cu-rich multielement alloy containing Zn, Sn, Ag, and Au was synthesized and studied to explore its structural and physical properties. The alloy was prepared by vacuum-sealed melting of high-purity elements followed by rapid quenching in cold water. Powder X-ray diffraction confirms that the alloy crystallizes in a face-centered cubic (fcc) Cu-type structure. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping show uniform distribution of all constituent elements. Magnetic measurements indicate the appearance of a superconducting transition at low temperature, while electrical resistivity remains metallic without reaching zero resistance. This difference between magnetic and transport behaviour suggests that the superconducting state may be limited to local or partial regions within the sample. These findings indicate that the Cu-rich multielement alloy exhibits unusual low-temperature properties and may represent a new class of compositionally complex Cu-based materials with superconducting characteristics.

summaries.en: A rapidly quenched Cu-rich multielement alloy containing Zn, Sn, Ag, and Au crystallizes in an fcc Cu-type structure with uniformly distributed elements and shows a low-temperature superconducting transition in magnetic measurements, although its electrical resistivity remains metallic without reaching zero, suggesting superconductivity is confined to local or partial regions.

title: Zero-field plasmon splitter: Controlled interaction between quantum anomalous Hall edge states
abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect provides chiral edge states without the need for an external magnetic field, but unlike in conventional quantum Hall systems, their trajectories cannot be readily controlled electrostatically. Here, we engineer Coulomb interactions between two spatially separated, counter-propagating QAH edge channels using a floating metallic island. Microwave measurements reveal frequency-dependent redistribution of injected edge plasmons between two output channels, demonstrating interaction-induced hybridization of the collective modes. A long-range interaction model quantitatively reproduces the response and reveals a very low plasmon velocity in the coupling region, strongly reduced by electrostatic screening. Our results establish engineered Coulomb coupling as a route to control collective excitations in QAH edge states and provide a building block for chiral plasmonic circuits and electron quantum optics in magnetic topological insulators.

summaries.en: A floating metallic island is used to engineer Coulomb interactions between two counter-propagating quantum anomalous Hall edge channels, producing frequency-dependent redistribution of edge plasmons between two output channels that is quantitatively described by a long-range interaction model with strongly screened, low plasmon velocity, establishing engineered Coulomb coupling as a route to control collective excitations for chiral plasmonic circuits and electron quantum optics.
summaries.zh: 利用一个悬浮金属岛在两条反向传播的量子反常霍尔边缘通道之间引入库仑相互作用，实现了边缘等离激元在两个输出通道间随频率变化的重新分配，并由长程相互作用模型定量再现，该模型中耦合区的等离激元速度因静电屏蔽而显著降低，从而确立了通过调控库仑耦合来控制集体激发、并用于手性等离激元电路和电子量子光学的途径。

title: Frequency-domain spin-wave logic gate based on three-magnon confluence
abstract: Spin-wave-based information processing provides a promising platform for low-power nanoscale computing by exploiting coherent magnon dynamics and intrinsic nonlinear interactions. A key advantage of wave-based processing for efficient miniaturization is the ability to perform operations in the frequency domain without requiring separate propagation paths for the input and output signals. Here, we demonstrate a frequency-domain spin-wave logic gate based on resonant, non-degenerate three-magnon confluence in an yttrium iron garnet nanowaveguide. Under resonant conditions, two input spin waves at different frequencies efficiently generate an output spin wave at the sum frequency, which occurs only when both input signals are present, thereby directly implementing an AND logic operation. We further show that the output intensity scales linearly with each input intensity and is therefore proportional to their product, enabling analog multiplication of two signals. These results demonstrate nonlinear magnon confluence as a versatile mechanism for frequency-domain spin-wave logic and analog signal processing.

summaries.en: The authors demonstrate a frequency-domain spin-wave logic gate in an yttrium iron garnet nanowaveguide that uses resonant non-degenerate three-magnon confluence to generate an output at the sum frequency only when both input spin waves are present, implementing an AND operation and analog multiplication since the output intensity is proportional to the product of the input intensities.
summaries.zh: 作者在钇铁石榴石纳米波导中演示了一种基于共振非简并三磁子合流的频域自旋波逻辑门，只有在两个不同频率的输入自旋波同时存在时才在和频处产生输出自旋波，从而实现AND逻辑运算，并且由于输出强度与两输入强度之积成正比，还能实现模拟乘法。

title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
abstract: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a topology-based framework that uses persistent homology and L1 distances between normalized persistence images of subvolumes and a large reference volume to assess the representative volume element scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed by plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy, finding that topological distance decreases exponentially with increasing volume and differs in scale-dependent behavior from porosity and specific surface area.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种基于拓扑的框架，利用持续同形性以及子体积与大型参考体积之间归一化持续图像的L1距离，评估由等离子体聚焦离子束-扫描电子显微镜重建的镍-氧化钇稳定氧化锆固体氧化物电池阳极的代表性体积元尺度，发现拓扑距离随体积增大呈指数下降，且其尺度依赖行为与孔隙率和比表面积不同。

title: Polariton tweezers
abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. We show that introducing targeted frequency detunings between the continuous-wave pumps strictly breaks the spatiotemporal symmetry of the system, converting the stationary macroscopic interference pattern into a dynamically moving conveyor belt. By precisely customizing these frequency detunings, the entire lattice - along with the electrostatically trapped electrons - can be rigidly driven in any arbitrary in-plane direction. This precise phase-matching mechanism bypasses the need for a net kinetic momentum transfer, establishing a robust, optically controlled platform for the long-range routing of charged particles and topological defects in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.
subjects: Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall) ; Other Condensed Matter (cond-mat.other)

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates dynamic polariton tweezers that use the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar exciton-polaritons, created by a non-collinear three-beam TE-polarized pump in a semiconductor microcavity, to trap and transport electrons across a two-dimensional electron system by tuning pump frequency detunings so that the hexagonal polariton lattice moves rigidly in any in-plane direction.

title: Inhomogeneous Synthetic Fluxes in Optical Lattices
abstract: Synthetic gauge fields in optical lattices are usually engineered to realize a uniform magnetic flux. Here, we propose a scheme to generate spatially inhomogeneous fluxes and demonstrate how such fluxes reshape the single-particle spectrum. Within Wannier--Stark-assisted tunneling, onsite modulation produces a plaquette flux that depends on the orientation of the static tilt, whereas laser-assisted tunneling (LAT) does not. Using LAT, two coherent Raman processes with different momentum transfers imprint a dimerized Peierls phase that alternates the flux between neighboring plaquettes of a square lattice while keeping the mean flux fixed. A bond-selective Raman phase extends the scheme to the kagome lattice, where a parameter $\xi$ redistributes the flux between triangles and hexagons at fixed flux per unit cell. The Hofstadter--Rammal spectrum of the bipartite square lattice retains chiral symmetry for all $\xi$, whereas the kagome lattice lacks this symmetry, and its flux periodicity and reflection symmetries survive only at special values of $\xi$. As $\xi$ is reduced, the anomalous Landau levels of the kagome singular flat band are compressed toward the flat-band energy and evolve into a degenerate zero-energy manifold at $\xi=0$ with compactly localized states. The dynamical structure factor, accessible through Bragg scattering, resolves this evolution as a Rydberg-like series of peaks whose spectral span tracks the width of the anomalous-level tower and vanishes as $\xi\to0$. We discuss the frequency resolution and temperature required for its observation.
subjects: Quantum Gases (cond-mat.quant-gas) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

summaries.en: The paper proposes a scheme using two coherent Raman processes with different momentum transfers to generate spatially inhomogeneous synthetic fluxes in optical lattices, showing that a dimerized Peierls phase alternates flux between neighboring plaquettes at fixed mean flux and that a bond-selective extension to the kagome lattice produces a tunable parameter ξ that redistributes flux between triangles and hexagons, with dramatic consequences for the Hofstadter-Rammal spectrum and the anomalous Landau levels of the singular flat band.

title: Neonatal EEG Seizure Prediction with Quantum Inspired Continuous-Variable (Bosonic) Reservoir Computing
abstract: We study short-horizon neonatal seizure prediction on Helsinki-style (HUH) preprocessed EEG feature tables using quantum-inspired reservoir computing. Under strict subject-wise cross-validation on imbalanced preictal--interictal windows, we test whether reservoir constructions shaped after (i) gate-based qubit dynamics and (ii) continuous-variable (bosonic/photonic) dynamics provide a practical sequence encoder relative to strong classical baselines. Both reservoirs are executed here purely in classical simulation on a single GPU; accordingly, we do not claim quantum advantage, but rather evaluate whether quantum-shaped dynamics act as useful, low-footprint random feature maps with a trained linear readout. We compare against Random Forests and RBF--SVMs, and report AUROC, AUPRC, per-subject AUPRC, expected calibration error, and stratified bootstrap confidence intervals. Across our experiments, the CV/bosonic reservoir is consistently competitive and can improve AUPRC over the baselines, while the gate-style reservoir is more sensitive to hyperparameters. These results suggest that quantum-inspired, photonics-motivated reservoirs can be practical sequence encoders for neonatal EEG feature tables under conservative subject-wise evaluation.
subjects: Medical Physics (physics.med-ph) ; Machine Learning (cs.LG); Quantum Physics (quant-ph)

summaries.en: Under strict subject-wise cross-validation on imbalanced preictal–interictal windows from Helsinki-style preprocessed neonatal EEG feature tables, a classically simulated continuous-variable (bosonic/photonic) quantum-inspired reservoir with a trained linear readout proved consistently competitive with Random Forests and RBF–SVMs and could improve AUPRC, while a gate-based qubit-style reservoir was more hyperparameter-sensitive, with no quantum advantage claimed.

title: Detectability of an orbital-angular-momentum-based gravitational wave detector
abstract: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) of light provides a new approach to probing gravitational waves (GWs) through transitions between OAM states. Here, we assess the detectability of an OAM-based GW detector by developing a readout scheme and evaluating its noise budget over the frequency range from $1~\mathrm{mHz}$ to $100~\mathrm{Hz}$, including laser-intensity noise, laser-phase noise, mode-impurity noise, and shot noise. For a symmetric superposition OAM state, the GW-induced transition amplitudes satisfy $\alpha_+=-\alpha_-^*$, whereas the noise-induced mode-crosstalk coefficients obey $n_+=n_-^*$. Hence, the GW-induced signal forms a differential-mode contribution, while laser-intensity and mode-impurity noises enter as common-mode contributions, enabling their suppression by the balanced detection. Under a fixed beam-waist constraint, a shorter arm permits a larger paraxial parameter, reducing the equivalent angular-noise strain sensitivity. We adopt an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $\gamma=0.1$, a laser power incident on the beam splitter of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, and a wavelength of $\lambda_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$. Using representative noise spectra, we find that, for GWs from an equal-mass binary black hole with source-frame component masses of $M_{\mathrm{src}}=10^{4}\,M_{\odot}$ at redshift $z=1$, balanced detection yields an SNR of $24.7$ for an imbalance parameter of $\epsilon=10^{-3}$ and $239$ for $\epsilon=10^{-5}$, with the sensitivity approaching the shot-noise limit in the latter case. These results highlight the importance of a compact optical configuration and strong common-mode rejection for realizing an OAM-based GW detector.

title: Highly polarized epithermal neutron beam using polarized 3He gas at J-PARC
abstract: We have realized a highly polarized epithermal neutron beam using an in-situ polarized 3He spin filter at the high-intensity pulsed neutron facility J-PARC. A neutron polarization exceeding 80% was achieved for epithermal neutrons with energies below 1 eV, including a polarization of 86.4 $\pm$ 0.5% for 0.75 eV neutrons, which corresponds to the resonance energy of the p-wave compound state in the 139La+n system. The spin filter consisted of a 20-cm-long, 3.2-atm 3He gas cell polarized on the beamline using a compact laser-optics system for spin-exchange optical pumping (SEOP). A 3He polarization of approximately 78% was stably maintained on the beamline for more than 100 hours. The polarized epithermal neutron beam developed in this work provides a powerful tool for studies of discrete symmetry violations, including measurements of enhanced parity violation in neutron absorption by medium-heavy nuclei such as 139La and searches for time-reversal symmetry violation in neutron-nucleus systems.

title: Characterization of Next Generation Power Over Fiber Systems under Cryogenic Conditions for Advanced Physics Instrumentation
abstract: The successful application of Power-over-Fiber (PoF) technology to power photon detection systems in DUNE prototypes operating under high-voltage and cryogenic conditions has laid the groundwork for the next generation of PoF systems operating in harsh environments. This paper presents the characterization of the main components of a new PoF system operating at 1470 and 1550 nm, including the measurement of the electrical-to-optical conversion efficiency of laser transmitters, the optical-to-electrical conversion efficiency of commercial optical power converters (OPCs), and the estimation of optical fiber attenuation under cryogenic conditions. In addition, a detailed characterization of the response of silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) to light leakage from optical fibers and OPCs is presented, using 808 nm as a reference to evaluate the reduction in the SiPM response at longer wavelengths. The results of this work provide a foundation for the development of next-generation PoF systems capable of powering electronics and electrical systems for future high-energy physics experiments. In addition, the electrical isolation, low-noise operation, and long-term reliability of PoF technology could motivate its application in other research fields requiring remote power delivery under cryogenic conditions, as well as in systems where infrared photons could affect their performance.

title: Animated Ultraviolet Holography via Programmable Nonlinear Phase Transfer
abstract: Dynamic and programmable control of ultraviolet (UV) light remains challenging because of conventional high material absorption and the limited functionality of optics such as lenses, mirrors or filters, and optoelectronic devices, such as spatial phase modulators, over the UV range. Here, by employing the concept of virtual metasurfaces based on arrays of programmable optical patterns on a 600-nm-thick lithium niobate film as the nonlinear medium, we demonstrate nonlinear phase transfer, generating programmable holography in the UV range. This arrangement provides a unique platform for generating animated holograms. A spatial light modulator encodes a computer-generated phase distribution onto a longer-wavelength pump beam, while second-harmonic generation transfers the programmed spatial phase to the UV field through the quadratic nonlinear interaction. Importantly, the nonlinear film serves as a simple frequency-conversion interface, eliminating the need for nanostructure patterning or direct UV spatial modulation. By incorporating the nonlinear phase relationship into the hologram design, we experimentally reconstruct six distinct UV holographic patterns, with normalised cross-correlation values ranging from 0.68 to 0.83, demonstrating reliable UV holographic image reconstruction. As a result, the dynamic updating of the SLM enables animated UV holograms at 10 Hz, demonstrating reconfigurable UV holography using the same nonlinear film. The system also supports tunable SHG emission from 350 to 390 nm and dynamic beam steering at approximately 20 Hz. The results demonstrate the potential of virtual metasurfaces to realise software-defined UV holography by transferring spatial programming across optical frequencies. This opens new opportunities for reconfigurable short-wavelength UV beam shaping and structured illumination, without the need for UV-compatible optics or optoelectronics.

title: Finesse evolution in a bichromatic cavity under blue and red resonant illumination in vacuum
abstract: The long-term performance of high-finesse optical cavities depends on the stability of their mirror coatings under vacuum and under continuous exposure to high circulating power. In cavities supporting multiple wavelengths, a central question is whether degradation at one wavelength compromises performance at another. Understanding this interplay is essential for those cavity quantum electrodynamics experiments that need diverse optical fields for cavity stabilization, trapping, and light--matter coupling. Here, we investigate wavelength-dependent degradation and recovery of a bichromatic cavity with high-reflectivity coating at 455 nm and 671 nm in vacuum. Cavity ring-down measurements reveal a decrease in the 455 nm finesse from 7.7*10^3 to 1.9*10^3 after 11 hours of continuous exposure to high circulating power. Simultaneous measurements show no measurable degradation at 671 nm. Continuous operation at 671 nm, instead, produces no measurable degradation at either wavelength under the tested conditions. Comparison of oxygen depletion and Avrami-type loss models indicates kinetics compatible with nucleation and growth, without uniquely identifying the microscopic mechanism. We demonstrate partial recovery of the finesse with illumination at 455 nm in air. Our results indicate a wavelength dependence of laser-induced optical damage in bichromatic cavities and provide an estimate of the blue light intensity that can be safely used in such cavities.

title: Coherent transduction and dynamical back-action between light and millimeter waves
abstract: Electro-optic transduction can bypass the loss and noise of electronic frequency conversion at millimeter-wave frequencies by parametrically converting signals onto low-loss, low-noise optical carriers, with coupling rates that grow with frequency. Exploiting this growth, however, requires shrinking both the millimeter-wave and optical resonators while preserving their quality factors and spatial overlap, which has not yet been achieved. Here, we demonstrate a triply resonant transducer whose optical and millimeter-wave resonators have comparable dimensions and minimal mode volumes. Coupled lithium niobate Fabry-Pérot cavities, with free spectral ranges above 650 GHz and quality factors up to $10^6$, form a photonic molecule integrated with a quarter-wave gold resonator at 263 GHz. The device reaches a vacuum electro-optic coupling rate $g_0/2\pi \approx 60$ kHz, six times larger than previous millimeter-wave transducers and sixty times larger than at microwave frequencies. The device optically detects room-temperature thermal millimeter-wave photons at effective occupancies below one, which also serve as a calibration tone for transduction efficiency. Coherent transduction reaches cooperativities approaching 0.3, corresponding to internal efficiencies around 67%, accompanied by electro-optic dynamical back-action that broadens or narrows the optical resonances. These results demonstrate the advantage and feasibility of the frequency scaling of electro-optic coupling, establishing an architecture for weak-signal sensing and quantum and classical networking.

summaries.en: Here, we demonstrate a triply resonant transducer whose optical and millimeter-wave resonators have comparable dimensions and minimal mode volumes.

title: BEEF: A Hybrid Integrated Photonic Simulation Framework
abstract: A Python framework is presented that retains first-principles electromagnetic modeling while extending simulation to devices whose length and geometric complexity place them beyond the practical reach of either method alone. The Bridged Engine for eigenmode expansion (EME) and finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) (BEEF) partitions a device into sections which are simulated using either EME or FDTD independently developed Maxwell solvers depending on what best suits each section's geometry, and cascades the resulting responses. BEEF calibrates the EME propagation constants against FDTD-measured phase accumulation, providing a mode identity verification diagnostic across solver interfaces. For a 2x2 multimode-interference splitter, the hybrid result agrees with full-device FDTD to within 0.59% (bar) and 0.76% (cross) across the C-band; a tapered variant agrees to within 0.87% and 2.01%, respectively. For a directional coupler, effective-index calibration reduces cut-position dependence 167-fold. A circuit-level cascade reproduces the measured Fabry-Perot resonance lineshape and free spectral range while exploring the coupler-length and arm-length design plane through post-processing of four cached simulations. Finally, we use BEEF to simulate a 167.3 um-long 4x4 MMI-based 90-degree optical hybrid that is computationally impractical for full-device FDTD, with a reduced-length variant confirming close agreement in transmission and relative phase.

summaries.en: A Python framework is presented that retains first-principles electromagnetic modeling while extending simulation to devices whose length and geometric complexity place them beyond the practical reach of either method alone.
