title: Nonperturbative theory of thin-vapor-layer linear optical properties: towards the optimal design of alkali-metal vapor nanocells
abstract: Hot alkali-metal vapors confined inside nanometer-thick spectroscopic cells are highly suitable media for miniature and cheap frequency standards, magnetometers and atomic sensors. Yet, their linear optical properties in case of low to moderate atomic densities are not fully understood. The primary reason for that is the complex, strongly nonlocal optical response of such systems to the incident resonant radiation arising as the result of the free motion of atoms and their collisions with the walls. To date, calculations of reflection and transmission spectra of these cells has been restricted to perturbation theory in atomic density for the case of quenching atom-wall collisions, which substantially limited the scope of their practical applications. Here we introduce the rigorous numerical approach for computing thin-vapor-layer spectra with an accurate account for the nonlocal optical response at arbitrary optical density and layer thickness. Our model predicts a density-dependent blue shift of the resonance that is absent in the first-order perturbative description. We show that its values are comparable to the natural linewidth of an atomic transition and, therefore, too large to be neglected in most use cases. Inspired by recent experiments, we then explore a wide range of vapor layer thicknesses and study how the reflectivity and its derivative with respect to the laser detuning depend on the layer thickness. Finally, we derive an approximate expression for the thickness at which the first derivative of the reflectivity reaches its maximum that agrees closely with the rigorous numerical model and reduces to the first-order analytical result. These results provide a practical design tool for nanometer-thick spectroscopic cells in different applications as well as a starting point for further development of the theory.

summaries.en: Here we introduce the rigorous numerical approach for computing thin-vapor-layer spectra with an accurate account for the nonlocal optical response at arbitrary optical density and layer thickness.
summaries.zh: 在这里，我们介绍了计算薄蒸气层光谱的严格数值方法，并准确解释了任意光密度和层厚度下的非局域光学响应。
summaries.ja: ここでは、任意の光学密度と層厚における非局所光学応答を正​​確に考慮して、薄蒸気層スペクトルを計算するための厳密な数値的アプローチを紹介します。

title: $^{85}$Rb electromagnetically induced transparency and absorption on two collinear $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ three-photon cascade schemes
abstract: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor. Using the cascade system $5S_{1/2}\rightarrow5P_{1/2}\rightarrow5D_{3/2}\rightarrow 25F_{5/2}$ in $^{85}$Rb, we explore two collinear laser-beam configurations. The detunings of the upper two lasers of the cascade system are varied. In both configurations, the probe transmission maps contain rich sets of EIT/EIA features and substructures. To explain these, we utilize a dressed-atom and a quantum Monte Carlo trajectory method. The latter includes 108 relevant fine- and hyperfine-structure levels and their magnetic substates, accounting for coherent optical drives, optical pumping, atom recycling, electromagnetic decays via the $5P_{J}$ levels, and velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions. We find quantum-trajectory solutions of the Lindblad master equation, which show good agreement with experimental data and aid in finding physical explanations for the observed spectra. To further explore collision-induced spectral features, collisional loss of EIT/EIA visibility, velocity-changing and hyperfine collisions, we acquire spectra in Rb cells with 50 and 500~mTorr of Ar gas. Our work is of interest to studies of multi-level EIT systems that underpin emerging quantum technologies, where accurate accounting of internal atomic structure, laser beam geometry, optical pumping, transit time, and collisional effects is critical.

summaries.en: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor.
summaries.zh: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor.
summaries.ja: We present a comprehensive study of three-photon electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and absorption (EIA) in room-temperature Rb vapor.

title: Optical Acceptance Testing of Serenity-S1 Boards for the CMS HGCAL Phase-2 Backend Electronics
abstract: The CMS Phase-2 upgrade includes a new high-granularity calorimeter. The calorimeter electronics will include around 300 Serenity-S1 FPGA boards that use Samtec FireFly electro-optical modules with a link speed of up to 25 Gbps. General production tests performed by the central Serenity group only validate the high-speed links via copper loopback cables. We present an optical acceptance test framework specifically designed for the calorimeter, providing comprehensive link and slow-control validation of installed FireFly modules under realistic operating conditions. This test combines loopback and board-to-board testing, extended bit error ratio measurements, and continuous module health monitoring within an automated workflow, delivering structured diagnostics and ensuring reliable large-scale system deployment.

summaries.en: We present an automated optical acceptance test framework for the roughly 300 Serenity-S1 FPGA boards with Samtec FireFly electro-optical modules in the CMS HGCAL Phase-2 backend electronics, combining loopback and board-to-board testing, extended bit error ratio measurements, and continuous module health monitoring to provide comprehensive link and slow-control validation under realistic operating conditions beyond the copper loopback tests of general production.
summaries.zh: 我们提出了一套专为CMS高粒度量能器Phase-2后端电子学中约300块配备Samtec FireFly电光模块的Serenity-S1 FPGA板设计的自动化光学校收测试框架，结合环回与板对板测试、扩展误码率测量以及持续的模块健康监测，在真实工作条件下提供全面的链路与慢控制验证，超越了通用生产测试中仅通过铜缆环回进行的验证。
summaries.ja: CMS高精細度カロリメータPhase-2後段電子回路向けに、Samtec FireFly電気光学モジュールを搭載した約300枚のSerenity-S1 FPGAボードを対象とした自動光受入試験フレームワークを提案し、ループバック試験とボード間試験、拡張ビット誤り率測定、継続的なモジュール健全性監視を組み合わせることで、汎用生産試験の銅ケーブルループバックのみを超え、実運用条件下でリンクとスローコントロールの包括的な検証を実現する。

title: Experimental demonstration of response-enhanced fiber Sagnac gyroscopy via imaginary weak-value amplification
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a 100-m long fiber Sagnac gyroscope employing imaginary weak-value amplification (IWVA) to enhance the optical readout response to rotation. A Sagnac-induced polarization phase is converted into a measurable spectral response through polarization post-selection and spectrally resolved detection. By varying the post-selection angle, we characterize the gyroscope response over the experimentally accessible rotation-rate range. The response increases systematically toward orthogonal post-selection, yielding a maximum experimental enhancement of approximately 13 times relative to a fixed reference configuration without postselection. Fast Fourier transform and Allan-deviation measurements further characterize the noise and stability of the gyroscope. Near-orthogonal post-selection reduces the equivalent rotation-rate fluctuations, with the minimum Allan deviation decreasing from $0.06~\mathrm{rad/s}$ for the reference configuration to $0.0091~\mathrm{rad/s}$ for the configuration exhibiting the maximum response enhancement, corresponding to an approximately 6.6-fold reduction. Low-frequency fluctuations of the broadband superluminescent diode source limit the long-term stability. These results demonstrate that IWVA provides a practical approach for response-enhanced fiber-based Sagnac gyroscopy and precision rotation sensing.

summaries.en: This paper experimentally demonstrates a 100-m fiber Sagnac gyroscope using imaginary weak-value amplification with polarization post-selection and spectrally resolved detection, achieving up to ~13-fold response enhancement and reducing Allan deviation from 0.
summaries.zh: 本文实验演示了一种采用虚弱值放大、偏振后选择和光谱分辨探测的100米光纤萨格纳克陀螺仪，实现了约13倍的响应增强，并将阿伦偏差从0.
summaries.ja: 本論文は、偏光ポストセレクションと分光検出を用いた虚弱値増幅による100mファイバーサニャックジャイロスコープを実験的に実証し、約13倍の応答増強とアラン偏差の0.

title: Non-Hermitian Theory of Surface Emitting Jackiw-Rebbi States
abstract: Topological interface states in open photonic systems combine spatial localization at domain walls with temporal confinement characterized by a radiative quality factor. Here, we develop a non-Hermitian Dirac formalism for surface-emitting Jackiw-Rebbi states in dielectric metagratings. We show how varying the local amplitude of the lattice perturbation shapes the complex Dirac mass profile, enabling control over the quality factors and far-field radiation patterns of the interface states, while preserving their topological character. Applying this framework to a metagrating with second-order Brillouin-zone folding, we design a spatially graded superlattice perturbation that supports interface states with quality factors exceeding 10$^4$ and Hermite-Gaussian beam emission. These results establish superlattice perturbations as a strategy for topological beam shaping and offer a route toward high-Q topological surface emitters.

summaries.en: A non-Hermitian Dirac formalism for surface-emitting Jackiw-Rebbi states in dielectric metagratings shows that grading the local lattice-perturbation amplitude shapes the complex Dirac mass and thereby controls the quality factors and far-field radiation patterns of topological interface states while preserving their topological character, enabling a second-order Brillouin-zone-folding design with quality factors above 10^4 and Hermite-Gaussian beam emission.
summaries.zh: 针对介电超光栅中面发射Jackiw-Rebbi态的非厄米狄拉克形式理论表明，通过改变晶格微扰的局域幅度来调控复狄拉克质量，可在保持拓扑性质的同时控制拓扑界面态的品質因子与远场辐射图样，并据此设计出品质因子超过10^4、可发射厄米-高斯光束的二阶布里渊区折叠超晶格结构。
summaries.ja: 誘電体メタグレーティングにおける面発光Jackiw-Rebbi状態の非エルミートDirac形式を構築し、格子摂動の局所振幅を変化させて複素Dirac質量を制御することで、位相幾何学的性質を保ちながら界面状態の品質因子と遠方放射パターンを操作できることを示し、2次のブリルアンゾーン折り返しを用いた設計で10^4を超える品質因子とエルミート・ガウスビーム放出を実現した。

title: Energy-Centroid Trembling near Exceptional Points in Photonic Time Crystals
abstract: In a photonic time crystal with a modulated Lorentz restoring coefficient, modulation reweights the potential energy of the polarization and loss drains its kinetic energy; when these sectors are offset within a pulse, the energy centroid trembles in every cycle while the Poynting-flux velocity stays bounded. Near the gap-edge exceptional point the mode geometry amplifies these offsets, and for a narrow-band pulse on one passband Floquet branch the trembling-velocity amplitude generically grows as the inverse square root of the momentum detuning, rounded by finite bandwidth. Loss modulated in phase or in antiphase with the restoring coefficient can change the trembling coefficient while the band-slope and Petermann coefficients barely move. In the lossy example studied, a forward field pulse launched with the polarization at rest exhibits delayed bursts near the beat recurrence after substantial energy loss, with monochromatic amplitudes following the inverse three-halves power of the detuning over the computed range. Intracycle energy exchange and preparation thus shape the centroid motion beyond what the band slope and the Floquet Petermann factor determine.

summaries.en: In a photonic time crystal with a modulated Lorentz restoring coefficient, the energy centroid trembles each cycle near the gap-edge exceptional point when potential and kinetic energy offsets occur within a pulse, with the trembling-velocity amplitude growing as the inverse square root of momentum detuning and intracycle energy exchange shaping the motion beyond the band slope and Floquet Petermann factor.
summaries.zh: 在具有调制洛伦兹恢复系数的光子时间晶体中，当脉冲内势能与动能出现偏移时，能心在每个周期内于带隙边缘例外点附近发生颤动，其颤动速度幅度随动量失谐的负平方根增长，且周内能量交换塑造了超出能带斜率和Floquet Petermann因子所决定的质心运动。
summaries.ja: 変調されたローレンツ回復係数を持つフォトニック時間結晶では、パルス内でポテンシャルエネルギーと運動エネルギーのずれが生じると、ギャップ端の例外点付近でエネルギー重心が各周期ごとに揺らぎ、その揺らぎ速度の振幅は運動量離調の逆平方根で増大し、周期内のエネルギー交換がバンド傾斜とFloquet Petermann因子だけでは決まらない重心運動を形作る。

title: Semi-classical analysis of noise squeezing in Kerr microresonators
abstract: Kerr microresonators are integrated nonlinear devices widely used to generate classical optical frequency combs and nonclassical states of light. In particular, they provide a promising platform for squeezed light sources, which are important elements of emerging quantum sensing, communication, and computing technologies. Designing such sources requires numerical tools that efficiently incorporate realistic device physics and noise processes. Here, we show that established semi-classical frameworks based on the Lugiato-Lefever equation and the Ikeda map, instrumental in the development of classical light sources, can also predict the quadrature-noise properties of squeezed light when vacuum fluctuations are properly included. We consider three canonical configurations producing two-mode quadrature squeezing, single-mode quadrature squeezing, and intensity difference squeezing. In each case, the semi-classical simulations produce quadrature variances and noise spectra in close agreement with the quantum theoretical predictions. These frameworks therefore provide practical tools for designing squeezed light sources, with the capability to incorporate additional noise mechanisms, nonlinear effects, and complex resonator arrangements. More fundamentally, our results show that key experimental signatures of squeezing can be modeled as phase-sensitive amplification of properly normalized vacuum fluctuations within stochastic semi-classical field equations. This observation helps distinguish squeezing properties accessible through semi-classical field evolution from those intrinsically requiring a full quantum description.

summaries.en: Semi-classical frameworks based on the Lugiato-Lefever equation and the Ikeda map, when vacuum fluctuations are properly included, predict quadrature variances and noise spectra of two-mode quadrature, single-mode quadrature, and intensity-difference squeezing in Kerr microresonators in close agreement with quantum theory.
summaries.zh: 基于Lugiato-Lefever方程和Ikeda图的半经典框架在正确纳入真空涨落后，能够预测克尔微谐振器中双模正交压缩、单模正交压缩和强度差压缩的正交方差与噪声谱，且与量子理论预测高度一致。
summaries.ja: Lugiato-Lefever方程式と池田写像に基づく半古典的枠組みは、真空揺らぎを適切に取り入れることで、カー微小共振器における二モード直交圧縮、単一モード直交圧縮、強度差圧縮の直交分散と雑音スペクトルを量子論の予測とよく一致する形で予測できる。

title: Unlocking Low-Frequency Laser Doppler Holography Spectra for Functional Retinal and Choroidal Microvascular Phenotyping
abstract: The low-frequency part of optical fluctuation spectra recorded by laser Doppler holography at a frame rate of 37~kHz is typically filtered out to reveal functional blood-flow waveforms in major retinal and choroidal vessels. We construct a time-varying spectral-excess (SE) distribution in capillary-associated territories by selecting complete cardiac cycles and applying successive spatial and beat medians in regions where vessels are unresolved and intermittent eye motion can dominate the signal. At each phase, spectral excess compares the integrated Doppler spectral area between two fixed low-frequency peaks near $\pm2$~kHz with a reference area defined by the high-frequency tail near $\pm18.5$~kHz. The resulting waveform, displayed against normalized cardiac phase, retains variation throughout the cardiac cycle and provides a basis for exploring its temporal organization. We summarize spectral-excess strength by the spectral excess index (SEI), defined as the temporal median of SE, and also describe an alternative evaluation after spectral pooling. A representative recording illustrates the construction. Physiological specificity and repeatability remain to be quantified.

summaries.en: The paper introduces a spectral-excess (SE) analysis of the low-frequency portion of laser Doppler holography spectra—otherwise filtered out—to construct cardiac-phase-resolved waveforms in unresolved retinal and choroidal capillary territories, summarized by a spectral excess index (SEI), with physiological specificity and repeatability still to be quantified.
summaries.zh: 该论文利用通常被滤除的激光多普勒全息光谱低频部分，提出光谱过量（SE）分析方法，在未能分辨的视网膜和脉络膜毛细血管区域构建心动周期相位分辨的波形，并以光谱过量指数（SEI）加以概括，其生理特异性和可重复性尚待量化。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、通常フィルタリングで除去されるレーザードップラーホログラフィスペクトルの低周波成分を用いてスペクトル過剰（SE）解析を導入し、未分解の網膜・脈絡膜毛細血管領域における心周期位相依存の波形を構築してスペクトル過剰指数（SEI）で要約するものであり、その生理学的特異性と再現性は今後定量化される必要がある。

title: Quantitative Analytical Spheroid Model for Scattering-Type Scanning Near-Field Optical Spectroscopy of Layered Samples
abstract: Scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) is a versatile tool for probing optical properties at deeply subwavelength scales. Its theoretical modeling, however, typically relies on computationally intensive numerical simulations or phenomenological analytical models, limiting quantitative spectral interpretation. In our previous work, we introduced an exact analytical solution for the quasi-electrostatic prolate spheroid model of s-SNOM for homogeneous bulk samples, combining the accuracy of numerical simulations with the efficiency of analytical approaches. Here, we generalize this framework to multilayer samples using two equivalent methods: a generalized image charge method and a Fourier integral method. The resulting exact spheroid model reproduces finite-element simulations within numerical precision while retaining the computational efficiency of an analytical model. We validate the model experimentally for poly (methyl methacrylate) layers of different thicknesses, showing that a single set of geometrical parameters simultaneously reproduces multiple demodulation harmonics and all measured thicknesses, unlike the finite dipole model. We further demonstrate its applicability to strongly resonant SiC layers on dielectric and photoexcited InAs substrates, where existing analytical approaches fail. The model provides an efficient quantitative framework for interpreting multilayer s-SNOM spectra and extracting local optical properties.

summaries.en: The authors generalize their exact analytical prolate spheroid model of scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy to multilayer samples via equivalent generalized image charge and Fourier integral methods, matching finite-element simulations and experiments on PMMA, SiC, and photoexcited InAs layers where existing analytical approaches fail.
summaries.zh: 作者通过等效的广义镜像电荷法和傅里叶积分法，将其散射型扫描近场光学显微镜的精确解析长椭球模型推广到多层样品，结果与有限元模拟一致，并在聚甲基丙烯酸甲酯、碳化硅和光激发砷化铟层上得到实验验证，而这些情形下现有解析方法均失效。
summaries.ja: 著者らは、散乱型走査近接場光学顕微鏡の厳密な解析的長楕円体モデルを、等価な一般化镜像電荷法とフーリエ積分法により多層試料へ拡張し、有限要素シミュレーションと一致すること、また既存の解析手法が破綻するPMMA、SiC、光励起InAs層において実験的に検証した。

title: Chiral Unidirectional Resonances Enabled by Complete Coherent Radiation Control
abstract: Optical resonances are commonly characterized by their quality factors, while their radiation exhibits richer properties associated with polarization and directional selectivity. Chiral and unidirectional guided resonances exploit complementary aspects of radiation, motivating a unified framework for controlling polarization and directionality together. Here we develop such a framework and introduce chiral unidirectional resonances (CURs) with arbitrarily high radiative quality factors and near-unity single-channel selectivity. We further extend this theory to guide the geometric design of arbitrary coherent emission states with prescribed radiative lifetimes. In addition, we establish scaling laws for the lifetime and radiation-state fidelity, and demonstrate robust chiral unidirectional emission over a finite momentum region. Our demonstrations provide a basis for single-sided circularly polarized light sources and polarization-matched optical coupling.

summaries.en: The paper develops a unified framework for controlling polarization and directionality of optical radiation and introduces chiral unidirectional resonances with arbitrarily high radiative quality factors and near-unity single-channel selectivity, extending to the geometric design of arbitrary coherent emission states with prescribed radiative lifetimes.
summaries.zh: 该论文建立了一个统一控制光辐射偏振与方向性的框架，提出了具有任意高辐射品质因子和接近 unity 的单通道选择性的手性单向共振，并将其推广至按预设辐射寿命设计任意相干发射态的几何设计。
summaries.ja: 本論文は光放射の偏光と方向性を統一的に制御する枠組みを構築し、任意に高い放射品質因子とほぼ1の単一チャネル選択性を備えたキラル単方向共鳴を導入するとともに、所定の放射寿命を持つ任意のコヒーレント発光状態の幾何設計へと拡張した。

title: Optimal Fan-Out and Break-Even Routing Loss in Waveguide-Integrated Ge-on-Si SPAD Arrays
abstract: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts. We quantify this trade-off with the asymptotic count-based information rate, which prices dark counts and dead time in one unit and is attained by an optimally weighted moment estimator. For a non-paralyzable pixel, the information per pre-dead-time signal event peaks at a signal rate $y^*=\sqrt{D(D+1/\tau)}$ with exact efficiency $(\sqrt{1+D\tau}-\sqrt{D\tau})^2$, which sets the optimal fan-out and a critical flux above which equal splitting is optimal. We then compare four routing architectures on 64 simulated 16-pixel arrays: an equal passive tree, static trees (uncalibrated, and an idealized calibration-informed benchmark), an ideal programmable tree, and a thermo-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) tree with 1.32 dB excess loss. Ideal programmability gains up to 15.9 dB over equal splitting at low flux. At one known flux, however, the calibrated static splitter beats the MZI tree by 0.14-2.7 dB, and the penalty tends to twice the excess loss when dark counts dominate. In ensemble-median worst-case regret, the MZI tree breaks even only for flux windows wider than 2.55 decades, and not within six decades above about 3.4 dB excess loss. Event-level Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the count statistics and the predicted estimator variances within bootstrap confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses cover dark-count level, heterogeneity, detector model and random seed. All results are simulations with representative literature parameters.

summaries.en: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts.
summaries.zh: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts.
summaries.ja: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts.

title: Nonlinear Dynamics in Periodically Distributed Fibre Amplification Systems
abstract: We investigate effects of longitudinally varying nonlinearity on periodically distributed amplification systems in optical fibres. Emphasis is made on configurations in which the nonlinear coefficient exponentially grows or decays along the propagation distance, while the group-velocity-dispersion (GVD) coefficient is held constant. Such systems are of practical relevance to the design of highly efficient nonlinear devices, including broadband light sources and advanced amplification schemes, where precise management of the interplay between the GVD, nonlinearity, and gain is essential. Adopting the known generic integrability condition, we derive exact analytical expressions for the evolution of the optical field in the presence of the tailored nonlinearity profiles and periodically distributed gain. The resulting periodic wavetrain solutions and their long-wave limit in the form of bright and dark solitons provide insight into the controlled enhancement or suppression of nonlinear effects under realistic amplification conditions. The robustness of these solutions is examined by introducing finite perturbations and directly evaluating their effects on the corresponding intensity profiles. The structural stability of solutions against deviations from the integrability condition is demonstrated too. Outcomes of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of the nonlinear pulse dynamics in engineered gain-managed fibres and offer guidance for the development of novel optical systems, where the spatial distribution of the nonlinearity is exploited to optimise the performance.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Mathematical Physics (math-ph); Pattern Formation and Solitons (nlin.PS)

summaries.en: The paper derives exact analytical solutions, including periodic wavetrains and bright and dark solitons, for optical fibre periodically distributed amplification systems with longitudinally varying nonlinearity that grows or decays exponentially while GVD remains constant, and examines their stability under finite perturbations and deviations from the integrability condition.
summaries.zh: 本文针对非线性系数沿传播距离指数增长或衰减、而群速度色散系数保持不变的光纤周期性分布放大系统，推导出精确解析解，包括周期波列以及亮孤子和暗孤子，并考察了这些解在有限扰动和偏离可积条件时的稳定性。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、群速度分散係数を一定に保ちつつ非線形係数が伝搬距離に対して指数的に増大または減衰する光ファイバーの周期的分布増幅系について、周期波列および明暗ソリトンを含む厳密な解析解を導出し、有限摂動や可積分条件からのずれに対する解の安定性を検討した。

title: Optical Magnetic-Field Gating of Photon Avalanching Quantum Processes
abstract: Highly nonlinear phenomena, where macroscopic changes are triggered by microscopic perturbations, are ubiquitous in complex systems ranging from epidemic spreading to neural networks. In optics, photon avalanching represents a prime manifestation of such highly nonlinear behavior, characterized by a steep nonlinear response (s) following an avalanche threshold. However, this nonlinearity is typically determined by material composition, making this behavior challenging to tune for adaptive sensing, imaging, and neuromorphic applications. Here, we demonstrate giant optical magnetic field gated threshold and nonlinearity in lanthanide doped nanoparticles. We exploit the distinct quantum selection rules of the avalanche process: while the energy looping cycles of excited state absorption and cross relaxation are primarily electrically driven, the seed excitation, ground state absorption, is a mixed transition permitting magnetic dipole interaction. By positioning the emitters within an optical standing wave to spatially partition the electromagnetic field, we tune the local magnetic to electric field balance to selectively regulate the seeding and amplification probabilities. This allows us to demonstrate an unprecedented dynamic range of control over the power threshold and nonlinearity, tuning the order from s = 15 to s = 62. Furthermore, we harness this spatial separation of electric and magnetic fields using tightly focused cylindrical vector beams to locally sculpt the nonlinearity of a single nanocluster, achieving sub wavelength super resolution imaging that substantially surpasses conventional photon avalanche imaging under Gaussian illumination. These findings establish the magnetic component of light as a practical knob to actively program nonlinear optical dynamics, sub diffraction nanoscopy, and critical quantum dynamics at the nanoscale.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates that the magnetic component of light can gate photon avalanching in lanthanide-doped nanoparticles, tuning the power threshold and nonlinearity order from s = 15 to s = 62 and enabling sub-wavelength super-resolution imaging that surpasses conventional photon avalanche imaging under Gaussian illumination.
summaries.zh: 该论文证明光的磁场成分可以调控镧系掺杂纳米颗粒中的光子雪崩过程，将功率阈值和非线性阶数从 s = 15 调节至 s = 62，并实现优于高斯照明下常规光子雪崩成像的亚波长超分辨成像。
summaries.ja: 本論文は、光の磁場成分がランタニド添加ナノ粒子における光子アバランシェを制御できることを示し、パワー閾値と非線形次数を s = 15 から s = 62 まで調整するとともに、ガウス照明下の従来の光子アバランシェイメージングを大幅に上回るサブ波長超解像イメージングを実現した。

title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. The classical EM simulations are complemented by a quantum model for plasmon-exciton coupling based on the macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED) framework, along with Holstein vibrations. The goals are to show how LSPR spectra and SPP dispersion curves/attenuation constants changes as the strength of the molecular/semiconductor electronic transition increases and the system evolves from an energy transfer limit to strong coupling, and to provide an understanding of the decay processes from both classical EM and MQED perspectives.

summaries.en: This Perspectives article uses classical electromagnetic simulations complemented by a macroscopic quantum electrodynamics model with Holstein vibrations to examine how localized surface plasmon resonances and propagating surface plasmon polaritons are modified by coupling to molecular or semiconductor electronic transitions as the interaction evolves from the energy transfer limit to strong coupling.

title: First-principles simulation of free-electron lasers with the Galilean electromagnetic particle-in-cell method: even harmonics of planar undulators
abstract: Free-electron laser (FEL) codes average the electron motion over the undulator period and add the radiation harmonics through on-axis coupling factors. This is accurate for the fundamental, but the even harmonics of a planar undulator, which vanish on the axis, are not modelled at all. We show that the Galilean electromagnetic particle-in-cell method (GEM-PIC), which resolves the electron motion within the undulator period and the carrier of the forward radiation field without a Courant limit, simulates FELs on two CPU cores at two to three times the cost of a time-dependent run of the averaged code GENESIS. The quasi-cylindrical code GEM-PIC-RZ reproduces the coherent spontaneous emission of a planar undulator in each azimuthal mode $m = 0$--3 to within 2\,\% of the radiation integral, and seeded amplifiers to within a few per cent of GENESIS run with the same physics. For a seeded planar FEL at 10.6\,nm it predicts 12\,MW of second-harmonic power at saturation, $1.1\times10^{-3}$ of the fundamental; this harmonic is absent from the averaged model. The unaveraged code Puffin, which has no space charge, gives a comparable level, 9 to 11\,MW for the space-charge-widened and the initial beam size, and the same transverse structure.

title: PETE: A Hybrid Photonic and Electronic Thermoelectric Device for Direct Heat-to-Electricity Conversion
abstract: Photonic heat engines can achieve high conversion efficiencies, but their far-field power density is constrained by the blackbody limit. Near-field devices overcome this limitation through photon tunneling across a nanoscale vacuum gap; however, the mechanical spacers required to maintain this gap introduce parasitic heat conduction. We propose PETE (Photonic and Electronic Thermoelectric), a hybrid solid-state architecture in which thermoelectric generator (TEG) legs replace passive spacers. The legs simultaneously maintain the near-field gap and convert conducted heat into electricity. We evaluate PETE using an indium tin oxide emitter, an indium arsenide photovoltaic cell, and TaFeSb- and ZrNiSn-based Half-Heusler thermoelectric materials. At a hot-side temperature of 977K, the device achieves a power density of 18.6 W$\cdot$cm$^{-2}$ at 19.76% efficiency. This power density is approximately twice that of either the standalone near-field thermophotovoltaic device or the standalone TEG, while the efficiency is 44% higher than that of the standalone TEG. The performance can be tuned through thermoelectric geometry and material selection, and its adaptability is demonstrated for a broad range of thermoelectric materials and operating temperatures. PETE provides a general strategy for recovering spacer-mediated heat leakage in near-field photonic heat engines.

summaries.en: PETE is a hybrid photonic-electronic thermoelectric architecture in which thermoelectric generator legs replace the passive spacers of a near-field thermophotovoltaic device, simultaneously maintaining the nanoscale vacuum gap and converting parasitic conducted heat into electricity, achieving 18.

title: Learned optical compression for single-pixel quantitative phase imaging
abstract: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) reveals optical path-length variations in transparent objects but typically relies on spatially resolved intensity measurements. Here we numerically and experimentally demonstrate learned optical compression for single-pixel QPI, jointly optimizing a diffractive encoder and a digital neural decoder to concentrate reconstruction-relevant phase information into a compact measurement vector. A single reconfigurable phase-modulation plane sequentially displays the learned encoding patterns, which are independent of the input object, each yielding one scalar intensity measurement. Operating at a visible wavelength, the experimental system reconstructs quantitative phase images of unknown objects with ~40-fold dimensional compression, using only 2.55% as many intensity measurements as reconstructed pixels. Experimental blind testing on handwritten digits and grating-like phase objects achieves mean Pearson correlation coefficients of 0.945 and 0.848, respectively. Benchmarking under the same measurement budget demonstrates substantially higher reconstruction fidelity than other encoding strategies, highlighting the advantages of learned optical compression. With the optical encoder fixed, decoder-only neural adaptation enables experimental transfer to previously unseen data distributions, extending the utility of the learned measurement representation. These results establish learned optical compression as a measurement-efficient and reusable framework for QPI, integrating phase-information compression into single-pixel intensity measurements while retaining adaptability to new data. This approach paves the way for low-data-rate phase imaging and sensing, with the potential to extend QPI to spectral regions where high-quality detector arrays are costly or unavailable.

title: LADA: A differential algebra-based simulation package for arbitrary-order charged-particle and light optics
abstract: LADA computes charged-particle and light-optical transfer maps by differential algebra in Python, with run-time order selection validated through order nine. It combines these established map methods with ATIMA-based stopping, straggling and scattering, the GLOBAL, CHARGE and ETACHA charge-state models, EPAX fragmentation, six-dimensional integration through measured or computed RF fields with reference-energy rebasing, and section-wise particle tracking with aperture and RF-window losses. Maps retain analytic dependence on external parameters; contraction with input moments gives beam observables and their sensitivities without particle tracking at each setting. Lattice import from COSY, MAD-X, Xsuite and MIRKO provides per-record status and comparisons with available codes. NumPy is the only required dependency. On the HHT benchmark, the optional compiled DA kernel on eight cores matches COSY in performance at orders 3 and 5 and is 1.8 and 2.9 times faster at orders 7 and 9. Applications include the SIBAF irradiation facility through CALINA, proton microscopy and beam-line studies at GSI and FAIR.

summaries.en: LADA is a Python differential-algebra package that computes arbitrary-order charged-particle and light-optical transfer maps, integrating ATIMA-based energy loss and scattering, charge-state and fragmentation models, six-dimensional RF field integration, and multi-code lattice import to yield beam observables and parameter sensitivities without repeated particle tracking.
summaries.zh: LADA 是一个基于微分代数的 Python 软件包，可计算任意阶带电粒子和光学的传输映射，并集成基于 ATIMA 的能量损失与散射、电荷态与碎裂模型、六维射频场积分以及多程序晶格导入，无需重复粒子追踪即可给出束流可观测量及参数灵敏度。
summaries.ja: LADAは微分代数に基づくPythonパッケージで、任意次数の荷電粒子および光光学の伝達マップを計算し、ATIMAベースのエネルギー損失・散乱、電荷状態・破砕モデル、6次元RF場積分、複数コードのラティス取り込みを統合して、繰り返しの粒子追跡なしにビーム観測量とパラメータ感度を求める。

title: Propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam with conserved topology
abstract: We report the generation and control of a propagation invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam through the digitally controlled superposition of a first-order petal- and Gaussian- mode each marked with orthogonal polarizations. We present a detailed analysis of the spatial and polarization profiles and unveil their intricate topological features, showing that they have properties that are invariant to the propagation dynamics, in addition to their preserved intensity. The differential Gouy phase between the spatial components is shown to rotate the great circle traced by the polarisation distribution on the Poincaré sphere. Finally, we assess the beams for laser cutting and optical trapping, highlighting the relevance of topological structured light to these applications.

summaries.en: Digitally superposing a first-order petal mode and a Gaussian mode with orthogonal polarizations generates a propagation-invariant one-dimensional flat-top vector beam whose intensity and intricate topological features remain unchanged during propagation, with the differential Gouy phase rotating the polarization distribution's great circle on the Poincaré sphere, and the beam is assessed for laser cutting and optical trapping.
summaries.zh: 通过数字控制将带有正交偏振的一阶花瓣模与高斯模叠加，可生成传播不变的一维平顶矢量光束，其强度和复杂拓扑特征在传播过程中保持不变，而空间分量间的古伊相位差使偏振分布在庞加莱球上描绘的大圆发生旋转，并评估了该光束在激光切割和光捕获中的应用。
summaries.ja: 直交偏光を付与した一次のペタルモードとガウスモードをデジタル制御で重ね合わせることで、伝播不変な一次元フラットトップベクトルビームを生成し、その強度と複雑なトポロジカル特徴が伝播中に不変であることを示すとともに、空間成分間のグイ位相差がポアンカレ球上で偏光分布の描く大円を回転させることを明らかにし、レーザー切断および光トラッピングへの応用を評価した。

title: Numerical Verification Limits of Asymmetric Intrastromal Hydrogel Reinforcement for Decentered Keratoconus
abstract: Spatially tailored intrastromal hydrogel scaffolds have been proposed for decentered keratoconus, but their mechanical and optical benefits require stringent numerical validation. We reanalyze conforming two-material finite-element benchmarks and earlier optomechanical screening calculations, distinguishing solver verification from constitutive adequacy and treatment efficacy. In a curved corneal-patch benchmark with a fixed-volume rectangular inclusion, the apparent peak-displacement benefit of an offset over a centered inclusion changes from -5.66% to +1.73% across four tetrahedral meshes, while absolute displacements remain strongly mesh dependent. On the finest mesh, the quadratic term in the Green-Lagrange strain tensor contributes about 18% of the root-mean-square magnitude of the linearized strain; the underlying finite-element solutions themselves remain linear elastic. Earlier optical screening was sensitive to corneal orientation, mesh refinement and wavefront-reference conventions and is not retained as validated evidence. These observations do not establish superiority of asymmetric reinforcement. Instead, they motivate prespecified criteria for geometry-invariant finite-strain simulations, two-material interface verification, optical wavefront convergence, and independent experimental validation. No clinical recommendation is implied.

summaries.en: Reanalysis of finite-element and optomechanical benchmarks for decentered keratoconus shows that apparent benefits of asymmetric intrastromal hydrogel reinforcement are highly mesh-dependent and do not constitute validated evidence of superiority, motivating prespecified convergence and experimental-validation criteria.

title: Experimental demonstration of phase-conjugated twin-wave coherent reception over 100 km with injection locking assisted phase stabilization
abstract: Recovering complex optical signals with high sensitivity is central to coherent communication and sensing. Beyond conventional homodyne and heterodyne reception, phase-conjugate twin-wave encoding and phase-sensitive joint detection offer an alternative strategy with enhanced sensitivity. Extending this approach to long-distance transmission of high-order-modulated signals is challenging because optical phase coherence must be maintained at the receiver. Here we experimentally demonstrate injection-locking-assisted phase-conjugated twin-wave reception of 200-MBaud signals with modulation formats up to 256-QAM over 100 km of optical fiber. Optical injection locking regenerates the local oscillator (LO) from a reference transmitted through the 16 dB-loss link, while pilot-assisted optical feedback stabilizes the relative signal-LO phase, enabling coherent combining of the phase-conjugated twin waves at a single balanced photodetector. At equal received signal-photon number per quadrature in each data-carrying optical mode, the measured PCTW signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exceeds the ideal single-mode homodyne standard quantum limit (SQL) benchmark. The SNR gains over the measured homodyne and conventional heterodyne results are about 3 dB and 6 dB, respectively. Constellation and bit-error-rate measurements show that this gain improves high-order data recovery relative to heterodyne reception. An ideal Gaussian-noise model predicts a photon information efficiency of 1.54 bits per received signal photon for uniform 16-QAM. These results establish an injection-locking-assisted coherent receiver architecture that implements joint detection of phase-conjugated twin waves over 100 km of fiber with enhanced sensitivity, providing a practical route for photon-efficient coherent communication.

summaries.en: By using injection locking to regenerate the local oscillator and pilot-assisted feedback to stabilize the signal-LO phase, the authors experimentally demonstrate phase-conjugated twin-wave coherent reception of 200-MBaud signals up to 256-QAM over 100 km of fiber, achieving about 3 dB and 6 dB SNR gains over homodyne and heterodyne reception, respectively, and exceeding the ideal homodyne standard quantum limit.

title: Controlling the Sign and Magnitude of the Thermoreflectance Coefficient of Gold-MoS$_2$ Metamaterials
abstract: Heating a material changes how much light it reflects. This effect, quantified by the thermoreflectance coefficient $C_\mathrm{TR}$, enables temperature sensing, while it is a nuisance for situations where constant reflection is crucial. Whereas temperature detection requires a large $C_\mathrm{TR}$, the latter situation demands it to be as close to zero as possible. Controlling the $C_\mathrm{TR}$ has so far relied on the selection of materials and wavelengths, rather than engineering the coefficient itself. This work demonstrates that the $C_\mathrm{TR}$ of a 50 nm thin gold film on SiO$_2$/Si can be controlled in sign and magnitude by an ultrathin ($<$8 nm) MoS$_2$ film underneath it. Time-resolved thermoreflectance measurements reveal suppression, sign inversion, and revival of the thermoreflectance signal, controlled by three knobs: ($i$) the buried MoS$_2$ thickness, ($ii$) probe wavelength, and ($iii$) ambient temperature. Transfer-matrix simulations using temperature-dependent dielectric functions of gold and MoS$_2$ reproduce all experimental observations, demonstrating an optothermal metamaterial platform with controllable properties. In particular, these (anti-)thermoreflective metamaterial mirrors bring $C_\mathrm{TR}$ under the same interference design rules previously applied to the optical response itself, opening ways to maximize or minimize the temperature dependence of the optical reflectance, tailored to the specific application.

summaries.en: This work shows that an ultrathin (<8 nm) MoS2 film buried under a 50 nm gold film on SiO2/Si allows the sign and magnitude of the thermoreflectance coefficient to be controlled via the MoS2 thickness, probe wavelength, and ambient temperature, forming an optothermal metamaterial platform whose thermoreflectance follows the same interference design rules as its optical response.
summaries.zh: 该研究表明，在SiO2/Si基底上的50 nm金薄膜下方引入超薄（小于8 nm）MoS2层，可通过MoS2厚度、探测波长和环境温度三个调控手段控制热反射系数的符号与大小，从而构建出热反射特性遵循与光学响应相同的干涉设计规则的光热超材料平台。
summaries.ja: 本研究は、SiO2/Si上の50 nm金薄膜の下に超薄（8 nm未満）のMoS2膜を設けることで、MoS2膜厚・プローブ波長・周囲温度の3つの制御因子により熱反射係数の符号と大きさを制御できることを示し、熱反射特性が光学応答と同じ干渉設計則に従う光熱メタマテリアルプラットフォームを実現した。

title: Scan-less Hyperspectral Polarimetric Imaging Using Dual-Comb Single-Pixel Imaging
abstract: Spectroscopic polarimetry enables detailed characterization of light-matter interactions by combining spectral and polarization information, yet conventional implementations rely on mechanical polarization modulation and are difficult to extend to fast, broadband imaging. Dual-comb spectroscopic polarimetry (DCSP) addresses these limitations by providing rapid, modulation-free access to polarization-resolved amplitude and phase spectra, but has so far been limited to point-based measurements. In this work, we introduce dual-comb spectro-polarimetric single-pixel imaging (DCSP-SPI), a new framework that combines DCSP with structured illumination and single-pixel detection to achieve scan-less hyperspectral polarimetric imaging without a camera. By exploiting the intrinsic amplitude and phase sensitivity of dual-comb interferometry, spectrally resolved images of the amplitude ratio psi and phase difference delta are reconstructed across a broad optical spectrum. The performance of DCSP-SPI is demonstrated through imaging experiments using a birefringent resolution target and a Fabry-Perot etalon, where frequency-dependent psi and delta images are obtained and shown to follow the expected spectral and polarization characteristics. Furthermore, the approach is extended to hyperspectral reconstruction of full Jones matrix elements by using multiple incident polarization states. The proposed DCSP-SPI framework provides a new pathway toward scan-less, hyperspectral polarization imaging, offering a flexible platform for applications requiring quantitative spatial, spectral, and polarization analysis.

summaries.en: The paper introduces dual-comb spectro-polarimetric single-pixel imaging, a scan-less camera-free framework that combines dual-comb spectroscopic polarimetry with structured illumination and single-pixel detection to reconstruct spectrally resolved images of the amplitude ratio psi and phase difference delta, and extends it to full Jones matrix hyperspectral imaging.

title: Optical spectral asymmetry enables differential refractive-index sensing under near-perfect common-mode suppression in a single-cavity dual-comb fiber laser
abstract: Single-cavity dual-comb fiber lasers offer near-perfect common-mode suppression, but such suppression is generally expected to eliminate differential sensing signals. Here we show that optical spectral asymmetry enables differential refractive-index (RI) sensing despite near-perfect common-mode suppression. By integrating an intracavity multimode interference (MMI) fiber sensor into a shared cavity, two counter-propagating combs are simultaneously generated and interrogated, enabling differential RI sensing based on the repetition-frequency difference ({\Delta}frep). This architecture achieves near-perfect common-mode suppression, reducing temperature-induced drift by more than two orders of magnitude compared with a conventional dual-cavity dual-comb system. Spectral analysis reveals that optical spectral asymmetry gives rise to asymmetric repetition-frequency responses through cavity dispersion, thereby providing the physical origin of the differential sensing signal. A trade-off between sensitivity and noise suppression is identified: while the sensitivity is reduced due to the shared sensor, the improved frequency stability enhances robustness against environmental perturbations. These results demonstrate that near-perfect common-mode suppression does not preclude differential sensing, but instead reveals a new sensing mechanism governed by optical spectral asymmetry. These findings establish optical spectral asymmetry as a design principle for differential sensing in single-cavity dual-comb systems and provide a framework for highly stable long-term photonic sensing.

summaries.en: Optical spectral asymmetry in a single-cavity dual-comb fiber laser enables differential refractive-index sensing via repetition-frequency differences despite near-perfect common-mode suppression, with cavity dispersion giving rise to asymmetric responses and greatly reduced temperature drift.
summaries.zh: 单腔双梳光纤激光器中的光谱不对称性使得在近乎完美的共模抑制下仍能通过重复频率差实现差分折射率传感，腔色散导致的不对称响应显著降低了温度漂移。
summaries.ja: 単一キャビティ型デュアルコムファイバレーザーにおける光スペクトルの非対称性により、ほぼ完全な同相モード抑制下でも繰り返し周波数差に基づく差動屈折率センシングが可能となり、キャビティ分散に起因する非対称応答が温度ドリフトを大幅に低減する。

title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors to evaluate TGVs

summaries.en: Holotomography nondestructively reconstructs the refractive index distribution of intact, unfilled through-glass vias to quantify their three-dimensional geometry, taper, and internal wall texture, separating slowly varying wall form from finer texture within a single optical inspection workflow.
summaries.zh: 全息断层扫描以非破坏性方式重建完整、未填充的玻璃通孔的折射率分布，从而量化其三维几何形状、锥度及内壁纹理，并在同一光学检测流程中区分缓慢变化的壁面形状与更精细的纹理。

title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sample preparation. This non-contact optical method achieves uncertainty below 5.3 * 10-8 K-1, substantially improving upon conventional thin-film CTE metrology.

summaries.en: An in-situ non-destructive optical method determines the coefficient of thermal expansion of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature dependence of their vibrational frequency, eliminating thickness measurements and achieving uncertainty below 5.

title: Dual-Space Analysis of Vortex Configurations and Rotational Energy in a 2D Optical Lattice
abstract: We investigate the effects of a stationary two-dimensional periodic optical lattice on a rotating Bose--Einstein condensate confined by an isotropic harmonic trap. Within the mean-field description, the condensate is modeled by the two-dimensional Gross--Pitaevskii equation in the rotating frame and solved numerically using an imaginary-time split-step Crank--Nicolson method to obtain stationary vortex states. We examine how the lattice depth, lattice wave vector, particle number, and angular velocity influence the vortex configurations, real-space density, momentum-space density, and energetics of the condensate. We find that the stationary periodic lattice significantly modifies vortex nucleation and spatial organization: vortices emerge progressively with increasing angular velocity and, for sufficiently strong lattice strength, undergo rearrangement and merging. Importantly, changes in the vortex configuration are directly reflected in the momentum-space density, demonstrating that vortex nucleation and rearrangement produce pronounced modifications of the condensate momentum distribution. We further analyze the energy per particle and rotational energy as functions of the angular velocity and find that the presence of the optical lattice substantially alters the rotational response of the condensate. In particular, the rotational energy is progressively reduced at higher angular velocities as the lattice strength is increased. These results demonstrate how a stationary periodic optical lattice modifies vortex formation, momentum-space structure, and rotational energetics of a rotating trapped Bose--Einstein condensate.

summaries.en: A stationary two-dimensional optical lattice significantly alters vortex nucleation, spatial organization, momentum-space density, and rotational energetics in a rotating trapped Bose-Einstein condensate, with increasing lattice strength reducing the rotational energy at higher angular velocities.

title: Deterministic and dynamic synthesis of optical skyrmions through an ultrathin multimode fibre
abstract: Topological light fields offer powerful opportunities for information encoding, transport, and manipulation, yet their deterministic generation in complex scattering media remains an outstanding challenge. In highly multimode fibres, strong mode coupling and polarisation mixing can obscure the precise control required to synthesise structured vectorial states, including optical skyrmions. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic generation and dynamic reconfiguration of arbitrary optical skyrmions through an ultrathin multimode fibre. By combining vectorial transmission-matrix control with a phase-retrieval optimisation framework, we exploit the full polarisation-resolved modal space of the fibre to reconstruct user-defined vector fields with high fidelity at the distal facet. This approach enables the synthesis of Néel, Bloch, anti- and higher-order skyrmions, and bimerons. Their topological properties are confirmed through polarisation-resolved Stokes-vector measurements and quantitative determination of the skyrmion number. Wavefront reprogramming further provides dynamic control over polarisation textures, enabling reversible transitions between distinct skyrmionic states. Our results establish multimode fibres as programmable platforms for the generation of topological light and introduce a scalable route towards minimally invasive topological photonics, with potential applications in imaging, sensing, optical communications, and information processing in complex environments.

summaries.en: By combining vectorial transmission-matrix control with phase-retrieval optimisation, this work deterministically generates and dynamically reconfigures arbitrary optical skyrmions, including Néel, Bloch, anti- and higher-order skyrmions and bimerons, through an ultrathin multimode fibre, with topological properties confirmed by polarisation-resolved Stokes-vector measurements and skyrmion-number determination.
summaries.zh: 本研究将矢量传输矩阵控制与相位恢复优化框架相结合，通过超细多模光纤确定性地生成并动态重构任意光学斯格明子（包括Néel型、Bloch型、反斯格明子、高阶斯格明子和双半子），并通过偏振分辨的斯托克斯矢量测量和斯格明子数定量确定验证了其拓扑性质。

title: Chiral phonon magnetism from localized Raman excitation
abstract: Optically driven chiral phonons can induce transient magnetism in non-magnetic crystals, yet the microscopic relationship between phonon angular momentum and the resulting magnetic response remains unresolved. Here we distinguish the roles of pseudo-angular momentum and mechanical angular momentum in tetragonal {\alpha}-TeO2. Combining phase-resolved terahertz spectroscopy with magneto-optical Kerr measurements (MOKE), we reconstruct the motion of a doubly degenerate phonon and continuously control its angular momentum. The MOKE response follows the sign and magnitude of phonon angular momentum as well as its dynamics, whereas non-rotating phonons, including those with finite pseudo-angular momentum, produce no detectable magnetic signal. The MOKE rotation corresponds to an effective magnetic field of approximately 14 mT, nearly seven orders of magnitude above the estimate for spatially uniform ionic currents. Moreover, the Kerr response scales linearly with the emitted terahertz field, rather than quadratically as predicted by the uniform-current model. A localized Raman-excitation model involving Te lone-pair states accounts for this scaling and yields a comparable field magnitude with the MOKE data when electronic enhancement is included. These findings identify mechanical lattice rotation as the dominant dynamical variable for the observed magnetic response and suggest that localized Raman coupling contributes to its unexpectedly large magnitude.

summaries.en: Phase-resolved terahertz spectroscopy and magneto-optical Kerr measurements on tetragonal α-TeO2 show that the Kerr response tracks the sign, magnitude, and dynamics of mechanical phonon angular momentum rather than pseudo-angular momentum, producing an effective field of about 14 mT that scales linearly with the emitted terahertz field and is explained by a localized Raman-excitation model involving Te lone-pair states.

title: Physics-Informed Surrogate for Sb2S3 Dispersion Trimming in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
abstract: A film-thickness error of 8 nm, within the tolerance of commercial thin-film lithium niobate wafers, shifts the group-velocity dispersion $\beta_2$ at 1550 nm by about 28 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$. We study numerically whether a segmented, non-volatile phase-change cladding can correct this error after fabrication. In mode solves of 3012 geometries, Sb$_2$S$_3$ switches $\beta_2$ by a median of 181 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$ at a 40 nm strip thickness with no material absorption under the adopted optical constants, whereas Sb$_2$Se$_3$ reaches a comparable contrast at a median modal loss of 5.6 dB cm$^{-1}$. Because phase adds along the guide, four independently switched binary segments reach a two-dimensional region of the $(\beta_2,\beta_3)$ plane; eigenmode expansion supports this description at the junctions. Full-wave solves at 65 die geometries show that the segment states move with the die error, so the bit pattern is chosen from a per-die model: a spectral surrogate constrained by exact identities of the lossless Maxwell problem. Its accuracy within the training domain is similar to that of unconstrained baselines; it keeps $\beta_2$ and $\beta_3$ consistent, and its error at an unseen film thickness is 8.3 rather than 13.0 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$. With a bare test ring and a second ring carrying a crystalline strip already on the mask, 96.8% of the dies are trimmed into $\pm25$ ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$, scored on full-wave solutions. A thermal model gives a candidate write window for a 532 nm beam.

title: Edge photocurrent distribution in luminescent solar concentrators: analytical treatment and solar cell arrangement
abstract: In luminescent solar concentrators (LSCs), the light flux along the edges is non-uniform, which causes current mismatch between series-connected edge solar cells. Here, the optical path distribution of photons arriving at an edge point was derived analytically for a rectangular LSC and generalized to convex polygons, with reabsorption and scattering included as a geometric series. The model agrees with Monte Carlo simulations and reproduces measured edge cell currents of a $60\times60$ cm$^2$ LSC within 2-3%. In a square LSC, the series mismatch reduces the current by 8-12% for four cells per edge. Rules for edge solar cell arrangement are formulated.

summaries.en: An analytical model of the photon optical path distribution at edge points of rectangular and convex polygonal luminescent solar concentrators, including reabsorption and scattering via a geometric series, matches Monte Carlo simulations and reproduces measured edge cell currents of a 60×60 cm² LSC within 2–3%, and it quantifies an 8–12% series mismatch current reduction for four cells per edge in a square LSC and yields rules for edge solar cell arrangement.

title: A plug-and-play platform for self-aligning 3D-printed structures on optical fibers
abstract: Two-photon polymerization 3D printing advances optical fibers into complex lab-on-fiber devices. However, widespread adoption remains bottlenecked by the inherent inefficiencies of sequential, direct-on-fiber printing. To address this, a custom-designed modular platform and a corresponding fiber-decoupled fabrication methodology on planar substrates are presented. This platform features a compliant, spring-like socket that enables passive self-alignment and reversible fiber insertion, paired with a customizable frontal device. The shift to fabrication on planar substrates enables parallel batch processing and allows the substrate to serve as a functional magazine for device mounting. To demonstrate this approach, modular platforms featuring a functional tip are printed, sharpened via post-process plasma etching, metallized, and equipped with an optical aperture using focused ion beam milling, while remaining on the planar substrate. Subsequently, these are used as exchangeable scanning probe microscopy tips mounted in situ within a scanning electron microscope. Simultaneous three-channel correlative imaging (atomic force microscopy topography, secondary electron, and cathodoluminescence) is used to validate the optomechanical stability of the design. Ultimately, by decoupling the delicate optical device's lifespan from the optical fiber, this architecture transforms lab-on-fiber tools into scalable, seamlessly replaceable consumables, offering a highly adaptable pathway for broader applications in photonics, sensing, and microscopy.

summaries.en: The paper presents a modular, self-aligning platform and fiber-decoupled fabrication method that enables parallel batch printing of 3D-printed lab-on-fiber devices on planar substrates for use as exchangeable, seamlessly replaceable consumable probes.

title: Electromagnetic Information Theory for Programmable Metasurfaces
abstract: Programmable metasurfaces enable fine-grained control of electromagnetic waves and are creating new opportunities for information extraction, information transfer and information processing. Yet, despite exciting experimental demonstrations, their fundamental capabilities remain poorly understood. In this Perspective, we argue that programmable metasurfaces, and programmable wave systems more generally, call for an electromagnetic information theory that addresses limits at two levels, in a unified manner across applications like communications, sensing and computing. First, for a given physical platform, such a theory should bound achievable information manipulations, such as sensing precision, information-transfer rates, and computational performance. Second, at a more fundamental level, it should determine what non-programmable and programmable physical resources bound these system-specific limits, and what minimum resources are required to attain a prescribed level of performance. We discuss emerging theoretical approaches to these questions, and their connection to experimentally realizable systems. We examine how device thickness, programmable degrees of freedom, nonlocality, coupling and multiple scattering constrain these limits. Establishing the envisioned framework could clarify the ultimate capabilities of programmable metasurfaces and guide the design of future wave-based information systems.

summaries.en: This Perspective argues that programmable metasurfaces and programmable wave systems require a unified electromagnetic information theory that bounds achievable information manipulations such as sensing precision, information-transfer rates, and computational performance, while identifying the physical resources—device thickness, programmable degrees of freedom, nonlocality, coupling, and multiple scattering—that constrain these limits and the minimum resources needed for prescribed performance.
summaries.zh: 这篇前瞻文章提出，可编程超表面及更广泛的可编程波系统需要一种统一的电磁信息理论，用以界定传感精度、信息传输速率和计算性能等可实现的信息操控极限，并确定器件厚度、可编程自由度、非局域性、耦合和多散射等物理资源如何约束这些极限以及达到既定性能所需的最小资源。
summaries.ja: 本パースペクティブは、プログラマブルメタサーフェスおよびより一般にプログラマブルな波動システムには、センシング精度・情報伝送速度・計算性能といった達成可能な情報操作の限界を規定するとともに、デバイス厚さ・プログラマブル自由度・非局所性・結合・多重散乱などの物理リソースがこれらの限界をいかに制約するか、および所定の性能に必要な最小リソースを明らかにする統一的な電磁情報理論が必要であると論じる。

title: Shot-to-shot statistical fluctuations during beam self-cleaning in multimode fibers
abstract: Beam self-cleaning in multimode optical fibers has recently been interpreted within a thermodynamic framework, in which nonlinear propagation drives the optical field towards a statistical equilibrium state. While this interpretation has been supported by measurements of modal populations and entropy, the role of shot-to-shot spatial fluctuations of the output beam has so far remained unexplored. Here, we experimentally show that the transverse output beam profile becomes progressively more reproducible from shot to shot as beam self-cleaning develops. This behavior is consistent with the thermodynamic expectation that relative fluctuations become increasingly small as the system approaches equilibrium.

summaries.en: Shot-to-shot spatial fluctuations of the transverse output beam profile in multimode fibers decrease progressively as beam self-cleaning develops, consistent with the thermodynamic expectation that relative fluctuations shrink as the system approaches equilibrium.
summaries.zh: 随着光束自清洁的发展，多模光纤中横向输出光束的逐脉冲空间涨落逐渐减小，这与系统趋近平衡时相对涨落变小的热力学预期一致。
summaries.ja: マルチモードファイバーにおけるビーム自己クリーニングの発達に伴い、横方向の出力ビームプロファイルのショット間空間揺らぎが徐々に減少し、これは系が平衡に近づくにつれて相対揺らぎが小さくなるという熱力学的予想と一致する。

title: Brillouin comb line amplifiers for optical atomic clocks
abstract: Optical atomic clocks outperform the microwave clocks at the heart of current timing and navigation infrastructure by orders-of-magnitude, and recent progress in on-chip integration provides the opportunity to widely deploy them. Conventionally, a narrow linewidth laser interrogates the atomic transition, and an optical frequency comb divides its stabilised frequency (hundreds of terahertz) down to a microwave that is electronically countable. The laser(s) impose a significant size, weight, power and cost penalty, which is a current barrier to low-cost, scalable, fully on-chip optical clocks. Here, we position the frequency comb as the central engine of the clock by using Brillouin-amplified comb lines for atomic spectroscopy, which eliminates the need for stable clock lasers. Amplified comb lines reach an ultra-low frequency noise floor of $6\,\mathrm{Hz^2/Hz}$ at $30\,\mathrm{kHz}$ offset, an order-of-magnitude below a high-end commercial fibre laser. We realize a clock based on the $\mathrm{5S}_{1/2}\rightarrow\mathrm{5D}_{5/2}$ transition in $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ with competitive fractional frequency stability of $2\times10^{-13}$ at $\tau = 1\,\mathrm{s}$, averaging to $9\times10^{-15}$ at $\tau = 1000\,\mathrm{s}$. Lastly, we demonstrate a photonic chip-integrated Brillouin amplifier with a record 62.9 dB gain and up to 40 dB transferred noise suppression when pumped with a simple, low-cost diode laser. This opens a new route to compact optical clocks and enables use of atomic transitions lacking low-noise lasers by broadening a comb to the required wavelength and amplifying single lines.

summaries.en: By using Brillouin-amplified comb lines for atomic spectroscopy instead of a stable clock laser, the authors realize a rubidium optical clock with a fractional frequency stability of 2×10⁻¹³ at 1 s and 9×10⁻¹⁵ at 1000 s, and demonstrate a chip-integrated Brillouin amplifier with 62.

title: Writing with Near-Field: towards Atomic Resolution in Material Processing
abstract: Direct laser writing with ultra-short pulses is the most flexible route to two- and three-dimensional (2D/3D) material modification, yet its resolution is judged against the optical diffraction limit. This review argues the opposite: the finest, most reproducible modifications come not from shortening the wavelength but from localising the absorber. Through the threshold effect and a transient epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) state - the dielectric-to-metal (Die-Met) state of the excited solid - the deposited energy is confined to a dipole-like nano-seed whose near-field intensity falls as r^-6 (ideal point dipole). The localisation is thus set by the seed size, not the focal wavelength, and the final feature is shaped by the material response: post-pulse heat flow, cavitation and quenching. We show that polarisation controls the anisotropy of deposition: the quasi-static near-field and interface boundary conditions select the writing direction and the modification orientation, down to a single defect. We survey energy-deposition mechanisms from 100 nm to the single-nanometer scale and link them to working engineering: stitch-free large-area patterning and record aspect-ratio (10^3-10^4) dicing and wafering of transparent crystals. Finally, we conjecture guided volumetric deposition, in which laser-inscribed lossy nano-seeds act as antennas that let cavity microwaves anneal the modified nano-volumes from within, as a 2.45 GHz oven heats food through water-dipole absorption. Throughout, atomic resolution is used in a quantum-confined sense and denotes a direction of travel: 10-20 nm features are demonstrated, while deterministic single-defect and single-bond modification remain goals. The thesis is that ultrafast direct write beats diffraction-limited intuition because the material itself forms a transient nanoscale absorber whose near-field and boundary conditions govern energy deposition.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Applied Physics (physics.app-ph)

summaries.en: This review argues that ultrafast direct laser writing achieves its finest, most reproducible material modifications not by shortening the wavelength but by localising the absorber, since threshold effects and a transient epsilon-near-zero (Die-Met) state confine deposited energy to a dipole-like nano-seed whose r^-6 near-field sets feature size and whose polarisation-dependent near-field and boundary conditions govern writing direction, enabling 10-20 nm features, stitch-free large-area patterning, and record aspect-ratio transparent-crystal dicing, with deterministic single-defect and single-bond modification remaining goals.
summaries.zh: 该综述提出，超快直接激光写入最精细、最可重复的材料改性并非源于缩短波长，而是源于对吸收体的局域化：阈值效应与瞬态 epsilon-near-zero（Die-Met）态将沉积能量限制在类偶极纳米种子中，其 r^-6 近场决定特征尺寸，且由偏振控制的近场与界面边界条件决定写入方向，从而实现 10-20 nm 特征、无缝大面积图案化以及创纪录深宽比的透明晶体切割，而确定性单缺陷与单键改性仍是未来目标。
summaries.ja: 本レビューは、超短パルス直接レーザー書き込みにおける最も微細で再現性の高い材料改質が波長の短縮ではなく吸収体の局在化に由来すると論じ、しきい値効果と過渡的なイプシロン近零（Die-Met）状態が堆積エネルギーを双極子的なナノシードに閉じ込め、その r^-6 の近接場がフィーチャーサイズを決め、偏光で制御される近接場と界面境界条件が書き込み方向を決めることで、10-20 nm のフィーチャー、継ぎ目のない大面積パターニング、記録的なアスペクト比の透明結晶ダイシングが可能となり、決定論的な単一欠陥・単一結合の改質は今後の目標であると示す。

title: Axion polarimetry with parametric readout: photon-number conversion and sensitivity limits
abstract: We propose a bias-assisted active photon-number conversion scheme for axion-induced polarization rotation in a four-port optical ring cavity with parametric readout. A calibrated real polarization rotation applied \emph{before} the final optical parametric oscillator (OPO) converts the otherwise quadratic response of the summed output photon number into a linear signal. We derive the resulting photon moments and the extracted-field covariance, retaining the four-port optical transfer, finite axion coherence and linewidth. Our principal phenomenological result is a prospective low-mass sensitivity window at $m_a=10^{-18}$--$10^{-16}\,\mathrm{eV}$, extending below the published exclusion bounds included in our comparison, notably the NuSTAR M82 limits. This is a conditional noise-equivalent projection, using the adopted $A/\sigma_A=1$ stochastic-power criterion and a parameterized technical-noise budget, not a confidence-level exclusion forecast. As a separate readout result, OPO-based total counting reduces the noise-equivalent coupling by approximately $5\%$ relative to matched selective attenuation in a favorable higher-frequency band; $5\%$ internal loss together with a $0.10$-rad pump-phase offset leaves a $3.5\%$ advantage in the stated example. A coherent input with only the final OPO retains this high-frequency benefit, whereas optimized coherent polarimetry remains more sensitive in the baseline. Our results identify both the operating principle of active number conversion and the stability requirements for a future implementation.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a bias-assisted active photon-number conversion scheme for axion-induced polarization rotation in a four-port optical ring cavity with parametric readout, showing a conditional low-mass sensitivity projection at m_a=10^-18–10^-16 eV and demonstrating that OPO-based total counting can reduce the noise-equivalent coupling by about 5% relative to matched selective attenuation in a favorable higher-frequency band.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了一种在四端口光学环形腔中利用参数读出实现轴子诱导偏振旋转的偏置辅助主动光子数转换方案，给出了在m_a=10^-18至10^-16 eV范围内的条件性低质量灵敏度预期，并表明在有利的高频波段中基于OPO的总计数相比匹配的选择性衰减可将噪声等效耦合降低约5%。

title: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy
abstract: Scientific applications of free electrons, such as in electron microscopes and particle accelerators, are limited by the brightness of available electron sources. Accelerators can use phase space cooling to surpass these source limitations, whereas electron microscopes can only rely on particle filtering to increase beam coherence at the cost of reduced brightness. We show that strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures makes it possible to achieve single-pass stochastic cooling inside an electron microscope for a lossless improvement of longitudinal emittance. This approach is laser-free and compatible with normal CW operation of electron microscopes. We derive a fully quantum mechanical model of stochastic cooling valid in the strong coupling regime, finding an analytic asymptotic formula for the optimal cooled energy spread $\sigma_{E_f}\simeq0.88(\hbar\omega)^{2/3}\sigma_{E_0}^{1/3}$, with $\hbar \omega$ the cooling photon energy and $\sigma_{E_0}$ the initial energy spread. Numerical simulations confirm that the energy spread reduction is reflected in an increase in the purity of the electron's quantum state and a reduction of the longitudinal phase space area. Our work paves a path towards even brighter beams for electron microscopy, promising higher image quality, enhanced spectral resolution, and a route to reaching fundamental quantum limits on electron beam phase space area.

summaries.en: Strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures enables single-pass, laser-free stochastic cooling inside an electron microscope, losslessly reducing longitudinal emittance and yielding an optimal cooled energy spread of approximately 0.
summaries.zh: 纳米光子结构中的强电子-光耦合使得在电子显微镜内实现单程、无激光的随机冷却成为可能，从而无损地降低纵向发射度，并得到约0.

title: Quantum simulation of real-time Yukawa dynamics with qubits and qumodes
abstract: Real-time quantum simulation of field theories offers access to scattering and decay dynamics, circumventing the limitations of Euclidean lattice methods. However, representing bosonic fields on qubits requires a finite-dimensional approximation and can entail costly multi-qubit operations. Hybrid qubit-qumode architectures avoid this by encoding bosonic fields directly in oscillators. We formulate scattering in the (1+1)-dimensional Yukawa theory for such a device, with staggered fermions on qubits and the scalar on qumodes. Trapped ions are a natural candidate, with the fermions on the internal states of the ions and the scalar on their collective motion, so that the Yukawa coupling becomes a native spin-dependent displacement. Emulating the device with tensor networks, we study the decay of a single scalar particle and fermion-antifermion scattering around the resonance region, using observables that can be measured on the device natively. We compare the results with those obtained using lattice perturbation theory. The emulation is able to resolve corrections beyond the Dyson summation of the one-loop self-energy.
subjects: Quantum Physics (quant-ph) ; High Energy Physics - Lattice (hep-lat); High Energy Physics - Phenomenology (hep-ph)

summaries.en: The authors formulate real-time scattering in (1+1)-dimensional Yukawa theory for a hybrid qubit-qumode device, with staggered fermions encoded in trapped-ion internal states and the scalar field in collective motion so the Yukawa coupling becomes a native spin-dependent displacement, and they emulate the device with tensor networks to study single-scalar decay and fermion-antifermion scattering near resonance, resolving corrections beyond Dyson summation of the one-loop self-energy.
